syād iti pūrvo gṛhṇīyāt pūrvaḥ sādayet pūrvo juhuyād etena vai vipūjanaḥ saurākiḥ pāpavasīyasaṃ cakāra tat pāpavasīyasam evaitena karoti yajñasya vai sṛṣṭasya śiro 'chidyata tasmai devāḥ prāyaścittim aichann atha vā etau tarhi devānāṃ bhiṣajā āstām aśvinā asomapau tā upādhāvan yathā bhiṣajam upadhāvanty evam idaṃ yajñasya śiraḥ pratidhattam iti tā abrūtāṃ bhāgo nā astv iti vṛṇāthām ity abruvaṃs tā abrūtāṃ grahaṃ nau gṛhṇantu somapītham aśnavāvahā iti tad vā aśvinau pratyadhattāṃ tasmād āśvinībhir abhiṣṭuvanty aśvinau hi pratyadhattāṃ tau vai bahiṣpavamānenaiva pāvayitvā tābhyāṃ pūtābhyāṃ yajñiyābhyāṃ bhūtābhyāṃ graham agṛhṇaṃs tasmād bahiṣpavamāne stuta āśvinau gṛhyete tasmād brāhmaṇena bahiṣpavamānam abhisṛpyaṃ pavitraṃ hi tat tasmād yaṃ dviṣyāt taṃ paribādheta tad vai bheṣajaṃ tredhā vinyadadhur agnau tṛtīyaṃ brāhmaṇe tṛtīyam apsu tṛtīyaṃ tad ya evaṃ vidvān agner ante brāhmaṇāya procyāpsu bheṣajaṃ karoti samardhukaṃ ha bhavati yāvad dhi bheṣajaṃ tat kriyate vāstuhāni vā etat pātrāṇi bhavanti yad grahān gṛhītvā bahiṣpavamānaṃ sarpanti vaiṣṇavya ṛcā punar etya saṃmṛśati viṣṇur vai yajño viṣṇunaivaināni yajñena svargaṃ lokaṃ samārohayati ||
4.6.2.d: यद् वै पात्रं रिक्तम् अनुन्मुक्तं तद् अनु रक्षांसि यज्ञम् अवयन्ति यद् ऐन्द्रवायवे पुरोडाशम् अवदधाति मैत्रावरुणे पयस्याम् आश्विने धानाम् अरिक्तत्वाय वि वा एतद् यज्ञश् छिद्यते यत् सवनानि संतिष्ठते यद् एतानि पात्राण्य् आ तृतीयात् सवनात् परिशेरे यज्ञस्य संतत्या अविछेदाय वायव्यायां शस्यमानायां पात्राणि विमुञ्चति प्राणो वै वायुः प्राणेन यज्ञः संततः प्राणेनैव यज्ञं संतनोति ॥ एकया च दशभिश् च स्वभूते द्वाभ्याम् इष्टये विंशत्या च तिसृभिश् च वहसे त्रिंशता च नियुद्भिर् वाय इह ता विमुञ्च ॥ इत्य् आह विमुक्त्या एवावगतं वा अध्वर्युपात्रं निरुद्धं प्रतिप्रस्थानं यदि कामयेत यो बहिस् तं ग्रामे कुर्यां यो ग्रामे तं बहिर् इति ॥ इदम् अहम् अमुम् आमुष्यायणम् अमुष्याः पुत्रम् अमुष्या विशो निरूहामि ॥ इत्य् अध्वर्युपात्रं निरुह्य ॥ इदम् अहम् अमुम् आमुष्यायणम् अमुष्याः पुत्रम् अमुष्यां विशि सादयामि ॥ इति प्रातिप्रस्थानं सादयेद् यो बहिस् तं ग्रामे करोति यो ग्रामे तं बहिर् अध्वर्युपात्रं वै यजमानस्य पात्रं प्रतिप्रस्थानं भ्रातृव्यस्य यदि कामयेत समावद्वीर्यम् एनं भ्रातृव्येण कुर्याम् इति प्रबाहुग् गृह्णीयातां प्रबाहुक् सादयेतां प्रबाहुग् जुहुयातां समावद्वीर्यम् एवैनं भ्रातृव्येण करोत्य् अध्वर्युपात्रं वै पात्रं पापीयः प्रतिप्रस्थानं यदि कामयेत पापवसीयसं स्याद् इति पूर्वो गृह्णीयात् पूर्वः सादयेत् पूर्वो जुहुयाद् एतेन वै विपूजनः सौराकिः पापवसीयसं चकार तत् पापवसीयसम् एवैतेन करोति यज्ञस्य वै सृष्टस्य शिरो ऽछिद्यत तस्मै देवाः प्रायश्चित्तिम् ऐछन्न् अथ वा एतौ तर्हि देवानां भिषजा आस्ताम् अश्विना असोमपौ ता उपाधावन् यथा भिषजम् उपधावन्त्य् एवम् इदं यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिधत्तम् इति ता अब्रूतां भागो ना अस्त्व् इति वृणाथाम् इत्य् अब्रुवंस् ता अब्रूतां ग्रहं नौ गृह्णन्तु सोमपीथम् अश्नवावहा इति तद् वा अश्विनौ प्रत्यधत्तां तस्माद् आश्विनीभिर् अभिष्टुवन्त्य् अश्विनौ हि प्रत्यधत्तां तौ वै बहिष्पवमानेनैव पावयित्वा ताभ्यां पूताभ्यां यज्ञियाभ्यां भूताभ्यां ग्रहम् अगृह्णंस् तस्माद् बहिष्पवमाने स्तुत आश्विनौ गृह्येते तस्माद् ब्राह्मणेन बहिष्पवमानम् अभिसृप्यं पवित्रं हि तत् तस्माद् यं द्विष्यात् तं परिबाधेत तद् वै भेषजं त्रेधा विन्यदधुर् अग्नौ तृतीयं ब्राह्मणे तृतीयम् अप्सु तृतीयं तद् य एवं विद्वान् अग्नेर् अन्ते ब्राह्मणाय प्रोच्याप्सु भेषजं करोति समर्धुकं ह भवति यावद् धि भेषजं तत् क्रियते वास्तुहानि वा एतत् पात्राणि भवन्ति यद् ग्रहान् गृहीत्वा बहिष्पवमानं सर्पन्ति वैष्णव्य ऋचा पुनर् एत्य संमृशति विष्णुर् वै यज्ञो विष्णुनैवैनानि यज्ञेन स्वर्गं लोकं समारोहयति ॥
4.6.2.m:
If a vessel is empty and unreleased, the evil spirits pursue the sacrifice into it.
When he places a cake in the Aindravāyava, curds in the Maitrāvaruṇa, parched grain in the Āśvina,
[it is] for the sake of non-emptiness.
The sacrifice is cut apart when the pressings conclude.
When these vessels lie around until the third pressing,
[it is] for the continuity of the sacrifice, for non-interruption.
While the [verse] to Vāyu is being recited, he releases the vessels.
Vāyu is breath;
by breath the sacrifice is continuous;
by breath indeed he connects the sacrifice.
'With one and with ten, O self-become one, with two for sacrifice, and with twenty,
and with three and with thirty you convey; O Vāyu, release those team-horses here,' he says,
just for the sake of release.
The Adhvaryu-vessel is gained;
the Pratiprasthātṛ's vessel is shut off.
If he should desire: 'Him who is outside may I make in the village, him who is in the village outside,' having drawn out the Adhvaryu-vessel with: 'Here do I drive out so-and-so, son of so-and-so, son of such-and-such a woman, from such-and-such a clan,' he should set down the Pratiprasthātṛ's vessel with: 'Here do I seat so-and-so, son of so-and-so, son of such-and-such a woman, in such-and-such a clan.'
Him who is outside he makes in the village; him who is in the village outside.
The Adhvaryu-vessel is the sacrificer's vessel;
the Pratiprasthātṛ's vessel is the rival's.
If he should desire: 'May I make him of equal power with his rival,' they should draw side by side, set down side by side, offer side by side.
He makes him of equal power with his rival.
The Adhvaryu-vessel is the vessel;
the Pratiprasthātṛ's vessel is the worse one.
If he should desire: 'May there be a disparity between better and worse,' the former should draw, the former set down, the former offer.
By this, indeed, Vipūjana Saurāki made a disparity between better and worse.
He thereby makes a disparity between better and worse.
When the sacrifice was created, its head was cut off.
The gods sought an expiation for it.
At that time, indeed, the two Aśvins were the physicians of the gods, not drinkers of Soma.
They ran to the two:
'As they run to a physician, so do you two replace the head of this sacrifice.'
The two said:
'Let there be a share for us.'
'Choose,' they said.
The two said:
'Let them draw a cup for us;
let us two partake of the drinking of Soma.'
The two Aśvins replaced it.
Therefore they praise with verses to the Aśvins;
for the two Aśvins replaced [it].
Having purified the two by means of the Bahiṣpavamāna, when they had become pure and worthy of sacrifice, they drew the cup for the two.
Therefore, when the Bahiṣpavamāna has been chanted, the two Āśvina [cups] are drawn.
Therefore a Brahmin should glide toward the Bahiṣpavamāna,
for that is a purifier.
Therefore, whomever he hates, him he should exclude.
They distributed that medicine in three parts:
a third in the fire,
a third in the Brahmin,
a third in the waters.
Therefore, he who, knowing thus, having declared [it] to the Brahmin at the edge of the fire, prepares the medicine in the waters, it succeeds;
for as much as the medicine is, so much is it prepared.
These vessels become left behind in an abandoned dwelling when, having drawn the cups, they glide to the Bahiṣpavamāna.
Having returned, he touches [them] with a verse to Viṣṇu.
Viṣṇu, indeed, is the sacrifice;
by means of Viṣṇu, by means of the sacrifice, he causes them to ascend to the heavenly world.

4.6.3.s: prajāpater vā ete cakṣuṣī yañ śukrāmanthinav asā ādityaḥ śukraś candramā manthī tasya vai prajāpateḥ savyaṃ cakṣur aśvayat tato ye stokā avāpadyanta tair idaṃ varṣaty ekaviṃśatir vai te 'vapedus tān vāyur amuto visṛjati prajānāṃ kḷptyai tasya yā kanīnikā parāpatat sa yavo 'bhavad yan manthinaṃ saktubhiḥ śrīṇāti cakṣur evāsya saṃbhāvayati mithunaṃ vai somaś ca saktavaś ca yan manthinaṃ saktubhiḥ śrīṇāti mithunatvāyārtaṃ vā etat pātraṃ yan manthipātraṃ yaṃ dviṣyād ṛtvijāṃ tasmai hared ārtim ārchati ṣaṇḍāmarkau vā asurāṇāṃ purohitā āstāṃ tān devā nāśaknuvan hantuṃ brāhmaṇavanto hy āsaṃs tau devā apāśāsur upa nā āvartethām iti tā abrūtāṃ bhāgo nā astv iti vṛṇāthām ity abruvaṃs tā etau śukrāmanthinā avṛṇātāṃ te devā amanyanta yad imā asuryau somau hoṣyāmas tad anv asurā ābhaviṣyanti yan na hoṣyāmas tad anv ābhaviṣyantīti tā apanudyāthendrāyājuhuvus tasmād etā anyadevatyau gṛhyete athendrāya hūyete apanuttau ṣaṇḍāmarkau saha tena yaṃ dviṣma iti ṣaṇḍāmarkayor evainaṃ sahāpanodenāpanudate || āyuḥ pāhi prajāṃ pāhy amuṣya vīratāṃ pāhi || iti sādayed yo 'sya priyaḥ syāt tasya śukraṃ vai prati rāṣṭraṃ manthinaṃ niruddhaṃ mathyatā iti hy etad rāṣṭram āhur yan niruddhaṃ bhavati yadi kāmayeta yo bahis taṃ grāme kuryāṃ yo grāme taṃ bahir iti || idam aham amum āmuṣyāyaṇam amuṣyāḥ putram amuṣyā viśo nirūhāmi || iti śukrapātraṃ niruhya || idam aham amum āmuṣyāyaṇam amuṣyāḥ putram amuṣyāṃ viśi sādayāmi || iti manthipātraṃ sādayed yo bahis taṃ grāme karoti yo grāme taṃ bahir ārtaṃ vā etat pātraṃ yan manthipātraṃ yañ śukrapātraṃ punaḥ prayujyate tasmād ime samāvadvīrye tasmād ābhyāṃ samāvat paśyaty asau vā ādityaḥ śukraś candramā manthī yad apidhāya prāñcā itas tasmād etau prāñcau yantau na paśyanty atha yad anapidhāya pratyañcau tiṣṭhantau juhutas tasmāt pratyañcau yantau paśyanti yad apidhāya prāñcā itas tasmāt parāṅ prāṇo 'tha yad anapidhāya pratyañcau tiṣṭhantu juhutas tasmāt punar apāno yad apidhāya prāñcā itas tasmāt parāñco garbhā dhīyante 'tha yad anapidhāya pratyañcau tiṣṭhantau juhutas tasmāt pratyañcaḥ prajāyante cakṣuṣī vai śukrāmanthinau nāsikottaravedir yad aṅguṣṭhābhyām ākramete cakṣuṣī vā etat pradhatto 'tha yad upariṣṭād ākramete tasmād ime upariṣṭāc cakṣuṣī tutho 'si janadhāyā devās tvā śukrapāḥ praṇayantv iti yā atrīḥ prajās tāsām eṣa yonis tā etam anuprajāyante tutho 'si janadhāyā devās tvā manthipāḥ praṇayantv iti yā ādyāḥ prajās tāsām eṣa yonis tā etam anuprajāyanta ubhayīr eva prajāḥ prajanayaty atrīś cādyāś ca śukram anvārabhante tejo vai śukro brahmavarcasaṃ teja eva brahmavarcasam anvārabhanta indreṇa manyunā yujeti śukreṇa pariyanti manyunā vai yujendro 'surān avābādhata manyunā vā etad yujā yajamāno bhrātṛvyam avabādhate saṃjagmānau divā pṛthivyety aratnī saṃdhatta imāni vā etat saṃdhatte yat pātre saṃdadhyātāṃ nedam antarā syād atha yad aratnī saṃdhattas tasmād idam antarā cakṣuṣor vidhṛtyai pumāṃsaṃ garbham ādhattaṃ gavīnyor iti tad anu strīṣvo yajamānasya gāvo bhavanti vīraṃ patnī janayati śukrasyādhiṣṭhānam asi manthino 'dhiṣṭhānam asīti śakalau prāsyataḥ samid vā eṣaitayor atho āhutīnāṃ pratiṣṭhityai nirastaḥ ṣaṇḍo nirasto markaḥ saha tena yaṃ dviṣma iti śakalau nirasyata etāvāṃl loko yāvad uddhataṃ yāvān eva lokas tasmād yajamāno bhrātṛvyaṃ nirbhajati śrīṇanty anyānt somān nānyāṃs tat somānāṃ mithunaṃ yāñ śrīṇanti tān anuvarṣati yān na śrīṇanti tān anuvīdhrati dārumayāny anyāni pātrāṇi mṛnmayāny anyāni tat pātrāṇāṃ mithunaṃ yo vai somasya ca pātrāṇāṃ ca mithunaṃ veda mithunā enaṃ paśavā upatiṣṭhante ||
4.6.3.d: प्रजापतेर् वा एते चक्षुषी यञ् शुक्रामन्थिनव् असा आदित्यः शुक्रश् चन्द्रमा मन्थी तस्य वै प्रजापतेः सव्यं चक्षुर् अश्वयत् ततो ये स्तोका अवापद्यन्त तैर् इदं वर्षत्य् एकविंशतिर् वै ते ऽवपेदुस् तान् वायुर् अमुतो विसृजति प्रजानां कॢप्त्यै तस्य या कनीनिका परापतत् स यवो ऽभवद् यन् मन्थिनं सक्तुभिः श्रीणाति चक्षुर् एवास्य संभावयति मिथुनं वै सोमश् च सक्तवश् च यन् मन्थिनं सक्तुभिः श्रीणाति मिथुनत्वायार्तं वा एतत् पात्रं यन् मन्थिपात्रं यं द्विष्याद् ऋत्विजां तस्मै हरेद् आर्तिम् आर्छति षण्डामर्कौ वा असुराणां पुरोहिता आस्तां तान् देवा नाशक्नुवन् हन्तुं ब्राह्मणवन्तो ह्य् आसंस् तौ देवा अपाशासुर् उप ना आवर्तेथाम् इति ता अब्रूतां भागो ना अस्त्व् इति वृणाथाम् इत्य् अब्रुवंस् ता एतौ शुक्रामन्थिना अवृणातां ते देवा अमन्यन्त यद् इमा असुर्यौ सोमौ होष्यामस् तद् अन्व् असुरा आभविष्यन्ति यन् न होष्यामस् तद् अन्व् आभविष्यन्तीति ता अपनुद्याथेन्द्रायाजुहुवुस् तस्माद् एता अन्यदेवत्यौ गृह्येते अथेन्द्राय हूयेते अपनुत्तौ षण्डामर्कौ सह तेन यं द्विष्म इति षण्डामर्कयोर् एवैनं सहापनोदेनापनुदते ॥ आयुः पाहि प्रजां पाह्य् अमुष्य वीरतां पाहि ॥ इति सादयेद् यो ऽस्य प्रियः स्यात् तस्य शुक्रं वै प्रति राष्ट्रं मन्थिनं निरुद्धं मथ्यता इति ह्य् एतद् राष्ट्रम् आहुर् यन् निरुद्धं भवति यदि कामयेत यो बहिस् तं ग्रामे कुर्यां यो ग्रामे तं बहिर् इति ॥ इदम् अहम् अमुम् आमुष्यायणम् अमुष्याः पुत्रम् अमुष्या विशो निरूहामि ॥ इति शुक्रपात्रं निरुह्य ॥ इदम् अहम् अमुम् आमुष्यायणम् अमुष्याः पुत्रम् अमुष्यां विशि सादयामि ॥ इति मन्थिपात्रं सादयेद् यो बहिस् तं ग्रामे करोति यो ग्रामे तं बहिर् आर्तं वा एतत् पात्रं यन् मन्थिपात्रं यञ् शुक्रपात्रं पुनः प्रयुज्यते तस्माद् इमे समावद्वीर्ये तस्माद् आभ्यां समावत् पश्यत्य् असौ वा आदित्यः शुक्रश् चन्द्रमा मन्थी यद् अपिधाय प्राञ्चा इतस् तस्माद् एतौ प्राञ्चौ यन्तौ न पश्यन्त्य् अथ यद् अनपिधाय प्रत्यञ्चौ तिष्ठन्तौ जुहुतस् तस्मात् प्रत्यञ्चौ यन्तौ पश्यन्ति यद् अपिधाय प्राञ्चा इतस् तस्मात् पराङ् प्राणो ऽथ यद् अनपिधाय प्रत्यञ्चौ तिष्ठन्तु जुहुतस् तस्मात् पुनर् अपानो यद् अपिधाय प्राञ्चा इतस् तस्मात् पराञ्चो गर्भा धीयन्ते ऽथ यद् अनपिधाय प्रत्यञ्चौ तिष्ठन्तौ जुहुतस् तस्मात् प्रत्यञ्चः प्रजायन्ते चक्षुषी वै शुक्रामन्थिनौ नासिकोत्तरवेदिर् यद् अङ्गुष्ठाभ्याम् आक्रमेते चक्षुषी वा एतत् प्रधत्तो ऽथ यद् उपरिष्टाद् आक्रमेते तस्माद् इमे उपरिष्टाच् चक्षुषी तुथो ऽसि जनधाया देवास् त्वा शुक्रपाः प्रणयन्त्व् इति या अत्रीः प्रजास् तासाम् एष योनिस् ता एतम् अनुप्रजायन्ते तुथो ऽसि जनधाया देवास् त्वा मन्थिपाः प्रणयन्त्व् इति या आद्याः प्रजास् तासाम् एष योनिस् ता एतम् अनुप्रजायन्त उभयीर् एव प्रजाः प्रजनयत्य् अत्रीश् चाद्याश् च शुक्रम् अन्वारभन्ते तेजो वै शुक्रो ब्रह्मवर्चसं तेज एव ब्रह्मवर्चसम् अन्वारभन्त इन्द्रेण मन्युना युजेति शुक्रेण परियन्ति मन्युना वै युजेन्द्रो ऽसुरान् अवाबाधत मन्युना वा एतद् युजा यजमानो भ्रातृव्यम् अवबाधते संजग्मानौ दिवा पृथिव्येत्य् अरत्नी संधत्त इमानि वा एतत् संधत्ते यत् पात्रे संदध्यातां नेदम् अन्तरा स्याद् अथ यद् अरत्नी संधत्तस् तस्माद् इदम् अन्तरा चक्षुषोर् विधृत्यै पुमांसं गर्भम् आधत्तं गवीन्योर् इति तद् अनु स्त्रीष्वो यजमानस्य गावो भवन्ति वीरं पत्नी जनयति शुक्रस्याधिष्ठानम् असि मन्थिनो ऽधिष्ठानम् असीति शकलौ प्रास्यतः समिद् वा एषैतयोर् अथो आहुतीनां प्रतिष्ठित्यै निरस्तः षण्डो निरस्तो मर्कः सह तेन यं द्विष्म इति शकलौ निरस्यत एतावांल् लोको यावद् उद्धतं यावान् एव लोकस् तस्माद् यजमानो भ्रातृव्यं निर्भजति श्रीणन्त्य् अन्यान्त् सोमान् नान्यांस् तत् सोमानां मिथुनं याञ् श्रीणन्ति तान् अनुवर्षति यान् न श्रीणन्ति तान् अनुवीध्रति दारुमयान्य् अन्यानि पात्राणि मृन्मयान्य् अन्यानि तत् पात्राणां मिथुनं यो वै सोमस्य च पात्राणां च मिथुनं वेद मिथुना एनं पशवा उपतिष्ठन्ते ॥
4.6.3.m:
The Śukra and Manthin [cups] are indeed the two eyes of Prajāpati.
Yonder sun is the Śukra;
the moon is the Manthin.
Prajāpati's left eye swelled.
The drops that fell down from it, by them it rains here.
Twenty-one [drops] indeed fell down.
Vāyu releases them from yonder for the proper arrangement of creatures.
The pupil that fell out of it became barley.
When he mixes the Manthin with barley-groats,
he thereby reconstitutes his eye.
Soma and groats are indeed a pair.
When he mixes the Manthin with barley-groats,
[it is] for the sake of forming a pair.
A stricken vessel, indeed, is this Manthin-vessel.
Whichever of the priests he might hate, to him he should carry it;
he meets with affliction.
Ṣaṇḍa and Marka were indeed the domestic priests of the Asuras.
The gods were not able to slay them,
for they were attended by Brahmins.
The gods called out to them:
'Turn toward us!'
They two said:
'Let there be a share for us.'
'Choose!' they [the gods] said.
They chose these two, the Śukra and Manthin [cups].
The gods thought:
'If we offer these two Asuric Somas,
the Asuras will prevail after that;
if we do not offer them, they will prevail after that.'
Having driven them away, they then offered [the cups] to Indra.
Therefore these two are drawn for another deity, and then offered to Indra.
'Driven away are Ṣaṇḍa and Marka together with him whom we hate'—
with the driving away of Ṣaṇḍa and Marka he drives him away.
'Protect life, protect offspring, protect the hero-power of so-and-so'—thus he should set it down for him who is dear to him.
The Śukra corresponds to the realm, the Manthin to one who is kept out: 'Let it be stirred,' for so they speak of a realm that is kept out.
If he should desire, 'Whosoever is outside, him may I put in the village; whosoever is in the village, him outside,'
having pushed out the Śukra-vessel with, 'Here I push out so-and-so, of such-and-such lineage, the son of such-and-such mother, from such-and-such clan,'
he should set down the Manthin-vessel with, 'Here I set down so-and-so, of such-and-such lineage, the son of such-and-such mother, in such-and-such clan.'
Whosoever is outside, him he puts in the village; whosoever is in the village, him outside.
A stricken vessel, indeed, is this Manthin-vessel.
Since the Śukra-vessel is employed again,
therefore these two are of equal virility;
therefore with these two he sees equally.
Yonder sun is the Śukra, the moon the Manthin.
Since, having covered [them], the two go eastward,
therefore people do not see these two going eastward.
Then, since, having uncovered [them], standing facing westward they two make the offering,
therefore people see them going westward.
Since, having covered [them], the two go eastward,
therefore the in-breath (prāṇa) goes forward.
Then, since, having uncovered [them], standing facing westward they two make the offering,
therefore the down-breath (apāna) comes back.
Since, having covered [them], the two go eastward,
therefore embryos are deposited facing forward.
Then, since, having uncovered [them], standing facing westward they two make the offering,
therefore they are born facing westward.
The Śukra and Manthin are indeed the two eyes;
the nose is the high altar (uttaravedi).
When they two step across with their two thumbs,
they thereby place the two eyes in front.
And when they step across from above,
therefore these two eyes are above.
'Thou art Tutha, the nourisher of people;
let the gods, drinkers of Śukra, lead thee forward'—
that is the womb of the creatures that eat;
they are born after this [formula].
'Thou art Tutha, the nourisher of people;
let the gods, drinkers of Manthin, lead thee forward'—
that is the womb of the creatures that are to be eaten;
they are born after this [formula].
He propagates both kinds of creatures: both those that eat and those to be eaten.
They take hold from behind the Śukra.
Śukra is brilliance, Brahman-splendour;
they take hold from behind brilliance and Brahman-splendour.
'With Indra as ally, with fury'—with the Śukra they go around.
With fury as his ally Indra pressed down the Asuras.
With fury as his ally the sacrificer presses down his rival.
'Uniting, with heaven and earth'—he joins the two forearms.
He joins these two; if they were to join the two vessels,
this [space] would not be in between.
And since they join the two forearms,
therefore this [space] is between the two eyes,
for separation.
'Place a male embryo in the two canals'—
following that, the cows of the sacrificer give birth to female calves and his wife brings forth a hero.
'Thou art the base of the Śukra;
thou art the base of the Manthin'—thus the two throw in the two chips [of wood].
That is the kindling-stick for these two,
and also for the firm establishment of the oblations.
'Cast out is Ṣaṇḍa;
cast out is Marka, together with him whom we hate'—thus the two cast out the two chips.
As great as the cleared ground is, so great is the world.
From as great as the world is, the sacrificer excludes his rival.
They mix some Somas, not others;
that is the pairing of Somas.
According to those that they mix, it rains;
according to those that they do not mix, it clears up.
Some vessels are of wood, others of clay;
that is the pairing of vessels.
Whoever knows the pairing of Soma and of the vessels, cattle in pairs wait upon him.

4.6.4.s: prajāpatir vā āgrāyaṇo ye devā divy ekādaśa sthety etāvanto vai devā yāvanta eva devās tebhyo gṛhyata āgrāyaṇaṃ vai gṛhītvā devāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyann apāsurā abhraṃśanta tato devā abhavan parāsurās tad ya evaṃ vidvān āgrāyaṇaṃ gṛhṇīte bhavaty ātmanā parāsya bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya ānujāvaraḥ syāt sa āgrāyaṇāgrān grahān gṛhṇītāgraṃ hy āgrāyaṇo yady abhicaret || vidad yadi saramā rugṇam adrer mahi pāthaḥ pūrvyaṃ sadhryak kaḥ | agraṃ nayat supady akṣarāṇām achā ravaṃ prahamā jānatī gāt || iti purorucaṃ kuryād rujati haivātho vāg vai saramā vācam evaiṣāṃ vṛṅkte sarā vā eṣā yajñasya tasmād yat kiṃca prācīnam āgrāyaṇāt tad upāṃśu caranty atha vā etad āgrāyaṇaṃ prati vācaṃ visṛjante yajñam evāptvā vacaṃ visṛjante vāg vai devebhyo 'pākrāmat te devās tūṣṇīṃ yajñam atanvata sā vāg amanyatāntar vai mā yajñād yantīti sāgrāyaṇaṃ prati nyādravat tasmād āgrāyaṇaṃ prati vācaṃ visṛjante hiṃkṛtya vācaṃ visṛjante prāṇo vai hiṃkāro vāk prāṇas tad vāca evaiṣa yuktis trir hiṃkaroti tredhā hīyaṃ vāg vadati śanair uccair atha sūccair yāvaty eva vāk sāsya yujyate trayo vai prājāpatyā ṛtvija udgātā prastotā pratihartā te vā asyaitarhy avṛttā ayuktā yad dhiṃkaroti tenaivāsya te vṛttā yuktā bhavanti vāk ca manaś cāvadetām ahaṃ śreyān asmy ahaṃ śreyān asmīti tau prajāpatiṃ praśnam aitāṃ sā vāg abravīn naiva mayā kiṃ canānabhyuditaṃ kriyatā ity atha mano 'bravīn naiva mayā kiṃ canānabhigataṃ kriyatā iti sa manase 'nvabravīt sā vāg abravīd ahavyavāḍ evāhaṃ tubhyam asānīti tasmād eṣā prajāpataye 'havyavāṭ tasmād yat kiṃcopāṃśu kriyate tad āhuḥ kṛtam etat kriyatā iti prajāpataye hi kriyate dvābhyāṃ dhārābhyāṃ prātaḥsavane gṛhṇāti tisṛbhyo mādhyaṃdine savane catasṛbhyas tṛtīyasavane tan nava nava prāṇā ātmāgrāyaṇaḥ prāṇān evātman dhatte vi vā etad yajñaś chidyate yat savanāni saṃtiṣṭhante ye devā divy ekādaśa stha pṛthivyām adhy ekādaśa sthāpsukṣito mahinaikādaśa stheti devatābhir vai yajñaḥ saṃtato devatābhir eva yajñaṃ saṃtanoti prajāpatir vā āgrāyaṇo yat sarveṣu savaneṣv abhipraskandayati prajāpatir vā etat prajā abhijighrati prajāpatir vā āgrāyaṇo yat sarveṣu savaneṣu gṛhṇāty ātmanaiva yajñaṃ saṃtanoti prajāpatir vā āgrāyaṇo yad eṣo 'tiricyate tasmāt puruṣaḥ paśūnāṃ daviṣṭham ety āgrāyaṇo vai gāyatryā vatsaras taṃ vā etad ā tṛtīyāt savanād abhipratidhāvati gāyatryā vā ete loke sarve somā gṛhyante tāṃ vā etat sarvāṇi savanāny abhipratidhāvanty atha yat sthālyā gṛhīto vijñātasthālyā hoṣyantī3 dārumayeṇā3 iti tasmād avijñātena garbheṇa bhrūṇahātha yat sthālīṃ riñcanti na dārumayaṃ tasmāt pumān dāyādaḥ stry adāyād atha yat sthālīṃ parāsyanti na dārumayaṃ tasmāt striyaṃ jātāṃ parāsyanti na pumāṃsam atha striya evātiricyante ||
4.6.4.d: प्रजापतिर् वा आग्रायणो ये देवा दिव्य् एकादश स्थेत्य् एतावन्तो वै देवा यावन्त एव देवास् तेभ्यो गृह्यत आग्रायणं वै गृहीत्वा देवाः स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन्न् अपासुरा अभ्रंशन्त ततो देवा अभवन् परासुरास् तद् य एवं विद्वान् आग्रायणं गृह्णीते भवत्य् आत्मना परास्य भ्रातृव्यो भवति य आनुजावरः स्यात् स आग्रायणाग्रान् ग्रहान् गृह्णीताग्रं ह्य् आग्रायणो यद्य् अभिचरेत् ॥ विदद् यदि सरमा रुग्णम् अद्रेर् महि पाथः पूर्व्यं सध्र्यक् कः । अग्रं नयत् सुपद्य् अक्षराणाम् अछा रवं प्रहमा जानती गात् ॥ इति पुरोरुचं कुर्याद् रुजति हैवाथो वाग् वै सरमा वाचम् एवैषां वृङ्क्ते सरा वा एषा यज्ञस्य तस्माद् यत् किंच प्राचीनम् आग्रायणात् तद् उपांशु चरन्त्य् अथ वा एतद् आग्रायणं प्रति वाचं विसृजन्ते यज्ञम् एवाप्त्वा वचं विसृजन्ते वाग् वै देवेभ्यो ऽपाक्रामत् ते देवास् तूष्णीं यज्ञम् अतन्वत सा वाग् अमन्यतान्तर् वै मा यज्ञाद् यन्तीति साग्रायणं प्रति न्याद्रवत् तस्माद् आग्रायणं प्रति वाचं विसृजन्ते हिंकृत्य वाचं विसृजन्ते प्राणो वै हिंकारो वाक् प्राणस् तद् वाच एवैष युक्तिस् त्रिर् हिंकरोति त्रेधा हीयं वाग् वदति शनैर् उच्चैर् अथ सूच्चैर् यावत्य् एव वाक् सास्य युज्यते त्रयो वै प्राजापत्या ऋत्विज उद्गाता प्रस्तोता प्रतिहर्ता ते वा अस्यैतर्ह्य् अवृत्ता अयुक्ता यद् धिंकरोति तेनैवास्य ते वृत्ता युक्ता भवन्ति वाक् च मनश् चावदेताम् अहं श्रेयान् अस्म्य् अहं श्रेयान् अस्मीति तौ प्रजापतिं प्रश्नम् ऐतां सा वाग् अब्रवीन् नैव मया किं चनानभ्युदितं क्रियता इत्य् अथ मनो ऽब्रवीन् नैव मया किं चनानभिगतं क्रियता इति स मनसे ऽन्वब्रवीत् सा वाग् अब्रवीद् अहव्यवाड् एवाहं तुभ्यम् असानीति तस्माद् एषा प्रजापतये ऽहव्यवाट् तस्माद् यत् किंचोपांशु क्रियते तद् आहुः कृतम् एतत् क्रियता इति प्रजापतये हि क्रियते द्वाभ्यां धाराभ्यां प्रातःसवने गृह्णाति तिसृभ्यो माध्यंदिने सवने चतसृभ्यस् तृतीयसवने तन् नव नव प्राणा आत्माग्रायणः प्राणान् एवात्मन् धत्ते वि वा एतद् यज्ञश् छिद्यते यत् सवनानि संतिष्ठन्ते ये देवा दिव्य् एकादश स्थ पृथिव्याम् अध्य् एकादश स्थाप्सुक्षितो महिनैकादश स्थेति देवताभिर् वै यज्ञः संततो देवताभिर् एव यज्ञं संतनोति प्रजापतिर् वा आग्रायणो यत् सर्वेषु सवनेष्व् अभिप्रस्कन्दयति प्रजापतिर् वा एतत् प्रजा अभिजिघ्रति प्रजापतिर् वा आग्रायणो यत् सर्वेषु सवनेषु गृह्णात्य् आत्मनैव यज्ञं संतनोति प्रजापतिर् वा आग्रायणो यद् एषो ऽतिरिच्यते तस्मात् पुरुषः पशूनां दविष्ठम् एत्य् आग्रायणो वै गायत्र्या वत्सरस् तं वा एतद् आ तृतीयात् सवनाद् अभिप्रतिधावति गायत्र्या वा एते लोके सर्वे सोमा गृह्यन्ते तां वा एतत् सर्वाणि सवनान्य् अभिप्रतिधावन्त्य् अथ यत् स्थाल्या गृहीतो विज्ञातस्थाल्या होष्यन्ती3 दारुमयेणा3 इति तस्माद् अविज्ञातेन गर्भेण भ्रूणहाथ यत् स्थालीं रिञ्चन्ति न दारुमयं तस्मात् पुमान् दायादः स्त्र्य् अदायाद् अथ यत् स्थालीं परास्यन्ति न दारुमयं तस्मात् स्त्रियं जातां परास्यन्ति न पुमांसम् अथ स्त्रिय एवातिरिच्यन्ते ॥
4.6.4.m:
The Āgrāyaṇa [cup], indeed, is Prajāpati.
'O gods who are eleven in the sky…' [he recites].
So many, indeed, are the gods;
for as many gods as there are, for them it is drawn.
Having drawn the Āgrāyaṇa, indeed, the gods went to the heavenly world.
The Asuras fell away.
Then the gods flourished; the Asuras were defeated.
Therefore, he who, knowing thus, draws the Āgrāyaṇa, flourishes himself; his rival is defeated.
He who might be born later should draw the cups beginning with the Āgrāyaṇa.
For the Āgrāyaṇa is the beginning.
If he should practice sorcery:
'If Saramā found the cleft of the rock, she made the great ancient path run together. / She who is swift of foot led the front of the syllables; knowing [the way], she went forth toward the roar'—
thus he should make the puroruc.
Indeed he cleaves [him].
Moreover, Saramā is speech;
he deprives them of speech.
She is the stream (sarā) of the sacrifice.
Therefore, whatever is prior to the Āgrāyaṇa, they perform that in a whisper.
Then, indeed, at the Āgrāyaṇa they release speech.
Having reached the sacrifice, they release speech.
Speech departed from the gods.
Those gods extended the sacrifice in silence.
That speech thought:
'They are excluding me from the sacrifice.'
She ran toward the Āgrāyaṇa.
Therefore, at the Āgrāyaṇa they release speech.
Having made the sound 'him', they release speech.
The sound 'him' is breath;
speech is breath;
that is the harnessing of speech.
Thrice he makes the sound 'him';
for threefold does this speech speak: softly, loudly, and then very loudly.
As far as speech extends, so far is it harnessed for him.
Three, indeed, are the priests belonging to Prajāpati: the Udgātṛ, the Prastotṛ, and the Pratihartṛ.
They, indeed, are not chosen, not hitched for him at this time.
When he makes the sound 'him',
thereby they become chosen and hitched for him.
Speech and Mind contended:
'I am better, I am better.'
They went to Prajāpati for a decision.
Speech said:
'Nothing at all is done without being uttered by me.'
Then Mind said:
'Nothing at all is done without being conceived by me.'
He decided in favor of Mind.
Speech said:
'I shall not be an oblation-bearer for you.'
Therefore, she does not bear oblations for Prajāpati.
Therefore, whatever is done in a whisper, about that they say: 'Let this that has been done be done,'
for it is done for Prajāpati.
With two streams he draws [it] at the morning pressing,
with three at the midday pressing,
with four at the third pressing.
That is nine.
Nine are the vital breaths;
the Āgrāyaṇa is the self;
he places the vital breaths in the self.
The sacrifice is cut apart when the pressings conclude.
'O gods who are eleven in the sky, who are eleven upon earth, who, dwelling in the waters, are eleven in greatness…' [he recites].
By the deities, indeed, the sacrifice is continuous;
by the deities he makes the sacrifice continuous.
The Āgrāyaṇa, indeed, is Prajāpati.
When he causes [it] to spill over at all pressings,
Prajāpati thereby sniffs at creatures.
The Āgrāyaṇa, indeed, is Prajāpati.
When he draws at all pressings, he makes the sacrifice continuous by the self.
The Āgrāyaṇa, indeed, is Prajāpati.
Because this remains over,
therefore man goes furthest of cattle.
The Āgrāyaṇa, indeed, is the year of the Gāyatrī;
toward it he runs back until the third pressing.
In the world of the Gāyatrī all these Somas are drawn;
toward it, indeed, all pressings run back.
Now, since it is drawn with an earthen vessel, [they say:] 'Will they offer with a distinct earthen vessel or with a wooden one?'
Therefore, through an unformed embryo [one becomes] a slayer of an embryo.
Now, because they empty the earthen vessel and not the wooden one,
therefore the male is an heir, the female is not an heir.
Now, because they discard the earthen vessel and not the wooden one,
therefore they discard an infant female, not a male.
And so females are left over.

4.6.5.s: indro vai vṛtrāya vajram udayachat sa vajram udyataṃ dṛṣṭvābibhet so 'bravīd asti vā idaṃ tyasminn antar vīryaṃ tat te pradāsyāmi mā mā vadhīr iti tad vā asmai prāyachad yajñaṃ vā asmai tat prāyachat paśūn ukthyam eva yad ukthyo gṛhyate yajñasya ca paśūnāṃ cāvaruddhyay etāvān vai yajño yāvān ukthyo 'ntaḥśleṣaṇam evānye grahāḥ plavo vā eṣa yajñasya yad ukthyo yathā vā idaṃ plavaṃ saṃnahya prasnāty evaṃ vā etad ukthyam ālabhya prasnāti sa enam ā yajñasyodṛcaḥ saṃpārayaty aṅgāni vā ukthyo yajñasya saṃtatyai gṛhyate tasmai tvā viṣṇave tveti viṣṇur vai yajño viṣṇunā yajñaḥ saṃtato viṣṇunaiva yajñena yajñaṃ saṃtanoty etena vā idam ukthāni saṃtatāni tasmāt puruṣaḥ snāvabhir anusaṃtataḥ sada ālabhyāvanayati yajñaṃ vā etat saṃtatya saṃprāpyāvanayati cakṣur vai śukraś cakṣur ukthyaś cakṣur vā etat purastād dhriyate 'tho yathedaṃ purastāt paścāt paśyann anvety evaṃ tad atha yad ekaḥ saṃs tredhā kriyate tasmād ekaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ pūrvārdhe 'vasyati yad etau grahau bhūyiṣṭhāḥ somā anu hūyante pāpavasīyasasya vyāvṛttyai yad etat pātraṃ bhūyiṣṭhāḥ somā anvāyanti tasmād ekaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yantaṃ bahavaḥ paścād anuyanti pātrāṇi vā adhvaryuṃ puro viduhra ukthāmadāni paścaindryā sadā upacaraty āgneyyāgnīdhraṃ vaiṣṇavyā havirdhānaṃ yathādevatam evaināny upacarati tathā hainaṃ na viduhre 'ntarāhavanīyaṃ ca havirdhānaṃ cādhvaryor loko 'ntarā havirdhānaṃ ca sadaś ca yajamānasya sadaḥ sadasyānāṃ yadi kāmayetādhvaryuṃ yaśa ṛched ity antarāhavanīyaṃ ca havirdhānaṃ cāvanayet somo vai yaśa eṣo 'dhvaryor loko 'dhvaryum eva yaśasārpayati yadi kāmayeta yajamānaṃ yaśa ṛched ity antarā havirdhānaṃ ca sadaś cāvanayet somo vai yaśa eṣa yajamānasya loko yajamānam eva yaśasārpayati yadi kāmayeta sadasyān yaśa ṛched ity antaḥ sadasyāvanayet somo vai yaśa eṣa sadasyānāṃ lokaḥ sadayān eva yaśasārpayati sada ālabhyāvanayaty aindraṃ vai sada aindrāṇy ukthāny ukthānāṃ saṃtatyay ukthānām anapachedāya || upayāmagṛhīto 'si mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ tvā || iti gṛhṇāti prātaḥsavane maitrāvaruṇāya || indrāya tvā || iti brāhmaṇāñśaṃsine || indrāgnibhyāṃ tvā || ity achāvākāya || upayāmagṛhīto 'sīndrāya tvendrāya tvā || iti gṛhṇāti sarvebhyo mādhyaṃdine savane || upayāmagṛhīto 'sīndrāvaruṇābhyāṃ tvā || iti gṛhṇāti tṛtīyasavane maitrāvaruṇāya || indrābṛhaspatibhyāṃ tvā || iti brāhmaṇāñśaṃsine || indrāviṣṇubhyāṃ tvā ity achāvākāyaivam asya yathokthaṃ yathādevataṃ gṛhītā bhavanti ||
4.6.5.d: इन्द्रो वै वृत्राय वज्रम् उदयछत् स वज्रम् उद्यतं दृष्ट्वाबिभेत् सो ऽब्रवीद् अस्ति वा इदं त्यस्मिन्न् अन्तर् वीर्यं तत् ते प्रदास्यामि मा मा वधीर् इति तद् वा अस्मै प्रायछद् यज्ञं वा अस्मै तत् प्रायछत् पशून् उक्थ्यम् एव यद् उक्थ्यो गृह्यते यज्ञस्य च पशूनां चावरुद्ध्यय् एतावान् वै यज्ञो यावान् उक्थ्यो ऽन्तःश्लेषणम् एवान्ये ग्रहाः प्लवो वा एष यज्ञस्य यद् उक्थ्यो यथा वा इदं प्लवं संनह्य प्रस्नात्य् एवं वा एतद् उक्थ्यम् आलभ्य प्रस्नाति स एनम् आ यज्ञस्योदृचः संपारयत्य् अङ्गानि वा उक्थ्यो यज्ञस्य संतत्यै गृह्यते तस्मै त्वा विष्णवे त्वेति विष्णुर् वै यज्ञो विष्णुना यज्ञः संततो विष्णुनैव यज्ञेन यज्ञं संतनोत्य् एतेन वा इदम् उक्थानि संततानि तस्मात् पुरुषः स्नावभिर् अनुसंततः सद आलभ्यावनयति यज्ञं वा एतत् संतत्य संप्राप्यावनयति चक्षुर् वै शुक्रश् चक्षुर् उक्थ्यश् चक्षुर् वा एतत् पुरस्ताद् ध्रियते ऽथो यथेदं पुरस्तात् पश्चात् पश्यन्न् अन्वेत्य् एवं तद् अथ यद् एकः संस् त्रेधा क्रियते तस्माद् एकः श्रेष्ठः पूर्वार्धे ऽवस्यति यद् एतौ ग्रहौ भूयिष्ठाः सोमा अनु हूयन्ते पापवसीयसस्य व्यावृत्त्यै यद् एतत् पात्रं भूयिष्ठाः सोमा अन्वायन्ति तस्माद् एकं श्रेष्ठं यन्तं बहवः पश्चाद् अनुयन्ति पात्राणि वा अध्वर्युं पुरो विदुह्र उक्थामदानि पश्चैन्द्र्या सदा उपचरत्य् आग्नेय्याग्नीध्रं वैष्णव्या हविर्धानं यथादेवतम् एवैनान्य् उपचरति तथा हैनं न विदुह्रे ऽन्तराहवनीयं च हविर्धानं चाध्वर्योर् लोको ऽन्तरा हविर्धानं च सदश् च यजमानस्य सदः सदस्यानां यदि कामयेताध्वर्युं यश ऋछेद् इत्य् अन्तराहवनीयं च हविर्धानं चावनयेत् सोमो वै यश एषो ऽध्वर्योर् लोको ऽध्वर्युम् एव यशसार्पयति यदि कामयेत यजमानं यश ऋछेद् इत्य् अन्तरा हविर्धानं च सदश् चावनयेत् सोमो वै यश एष यजमानस्य लोको यजमानम् एव यशसार्पयति यदि कामयेत सदस्यान् यश ऋछेद् इत्य् अन्तः सदस्यावनयेत् सोमो वै यश एष सदस्यानां लोकः सदयान् एव यशसार्पयति सद आलभ्यावनयत्य् ऐन्द्रं वै सद ऐन्द्राण्य् उक्थान्य् उक्थानां संतत्यय् उक्थानाम् अनपछेदाय ॥ उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि मित्रावरुणाभ्यां त्वा ॥ इति गृह्णाति प्रातःसवने मैत्रावरुणाय ॥ इन्द्राय त्वा ॥ इति ब्राह्मणाञ्शंसिने ॥ इन्द्राग्निभ्यां त्वा ॥ इत्य् अछावाकाय ॥ उपयामगृहीतो ऽसीन्द्राय त्वेन्द्राय त्वा ॥ इति गृह्णाति सर्वेभ्यो माध्यंदिने सवने ॥ उपयामगृहीतो ऽसीन्द्रावरुणाभ्यां त्वा ॥ इति गृह्णाति तृतीयसवने मैत्रावरुणाय ॥ इन्द्राबृहस्पतिभ्यां त्वा ॥ इति ब्राह्मणाञ्शंसिने ॥ इन्द्राविष्णुभ्यां त्वा इत्य् अछावाकायैवम् अस्य यथोक्थं यथादेवतं गृहीता भवन्ति ॥
4.6.5.m:
Indra raised his thunderbolt against Vṛtra.
Seeing the thunderbolt raised, he was afraid.
He said:
'There is indeed this virility within that one.
I will give that to you;
do not slay me.'
He gave it to him.
He gave him the sacrifice, cattle, the Ukthya indeed.
When the Ukthya is drawn,
[it is] to obtain the sacrifice and cattle.
The sacrifice is as great as the Ukthya.
The other cups are merely internal joints.
The Ukthya is indeed the boat of the sacrifice.
Just as one swims forth having tied together a boat here, so indeed having taken hold of the Ukthya he swims forth.
It brings him safely to the conclusion of the sacrifice.
The Ukthya is indeed the limbs.
It is drawn for the continuity of the sacrifice.
'For that one thee, for Viṣṇu thee' [he says].
Viṣṇu is the sacrifice.
By Viṣṇu the sacrifice is continuous.
By Viṣṇu indeed, by the sacrifice, he connects the sacrifice.
By this indeed these ukthas are continuous;
therefore a man is continuous along his sinews.
Having taken hold of the sadas, he pours [it] down.
Having connected the sacrifice, having reached it, he thus pours [it] down.
The Śukra is the eye;
the Ukthya is the eye.
The eye is thus held in front.
Moreover, just as one, seeing from behind, follows after what is in front, so is that.
Now, since being one it is made threefold,
therefore one foremost settles in the eastern half.
When the most somas are offered following these two cups,
[it is] for the separation of the worse and the better.
When the most somas follow this vessel,
therefore many follow behind one foremost who goes.
The vessels indeed milk the Adhvaryu in front,
the ukthamadhas behind.
He approaches the sadas with a verse to Indra,
the Āgnīdhra with one to Agni,
the Havirdhāna with one to Viṣṇu.
He approaches them according to their deities;
thus they do not milk him.
Between the Āhavanīya and the Havirdhāna is the Adhvaryu's space;
between the Havirdhāna and the sadas is the sacrificer's;
the sadas is the sadasyas'.
If he should desire: 'May glory come to the Adhvaryu,' he should pour [it] down between the Āhavanīya and the Havirdhāna.
Soma is glory;
this is the Adhvaryu's space;
he endows the Adhvaryu with glory.
If he should desire: 'May glory come to the sacrificer,' he should pour [it] down between the Havirdhāna and the sadas.
Soma is glory;
this is the sacrificer's space;
he endows the sacrificer with glory.
If he should desire: 'May glory come to the sadasyas,' he should pour [it] down inside the sadas.
Soma is glory;
this is the sadasyas' space;
he endows the sadasyas with glory.
Having taken hold of the sadas, he pours [it] down.
The sadas belongs to Indra;
the ukthas belong to Indra;
[it is] for the continuity of the ukthas,
for the non-interruption of the ukthas.
'Thou art taken with a support; / thee for Mitra and Varuṇa'—
thus he draws at the morning pressing for the Maitrāvaruṇa.
'Thee for Indra'—
thus for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
'Thee for Indra and Agni'—
thus for the Acchāvāka.
'Thou art taken with a support; / thee for Indra, thee for Indra'—
thus he draws for all at the midday pressing.
'Thou art taken with a support; / thee for Indra and Varuṇa'—
thus he draws at the third pressing for the Maitrāvaruṇa.
'Thee for Indra and Bṛhaspati'—
thus for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
'Thee for Indra and Viṣṇu'—thus for the Acchāvāka.
Thus for him they are drawn according to their ukthas, according to their deities.

4.6.6.s: āyur vai dhruvas tam uttamaṃ gṛhṇāty uttamaṃ hy āyuḥ sthālyā gṛhṇāty āyuṣo dhṛtyai pūrṇaṃ gṛhṇāti sarvam āyur eti prāṇo vai gāyatry āyur dhruvo yad eṣa ā tṛtīyāt savanāt pariśaye tasmād yāvad āyus tāvān prāṇa āyur vai dhruvo yad agniṣṭomam āsta āyur evāptvā niḥsarpaty āyur vai dhruvo yat kevalaṃ juhuyād āyuḥ prajānāṃ pradadhyāt paridhānīyāyāṃ śasyamānāyām avanayati sa hy anto hotuś camase 'vanayati vaiśvadevo vai hotā vaiśvadevīr imāḥ prajāḥ sarvāsu vā etat prajāsv āyur dadhāti janānām ity āhuḥ sarvāsāṃ vā etat prajānām āyuḥ sarvābhyaḥ prajābhyo gṛhyata ubhayatovaiśvānaro gṛhyata ubhayatovaiśvānaro hy ayaṃ prāṇo 'yaṃ vāva vaiśvānaro yo 'yam avāṅ prāṇo yad eṣa kevalā uttare havirdhāne sādyate tasmād eṣo 'rdhabhāk prāṇānām ardhabhājā itare hiraṇye 'dhi sādayed āyuḥkāmasyāmṛtaṃ vai hiraṇyam āyur dhruvo 'mṛta evāsyāyur dadhāty upopte 'nye grahāḥ sādyante 'nupopte dhruvas tasmād asthnānye paśavaḥ pratitiṣṭhanti māṃsena puruṣaḥ prāṇā vā uparavā yad eta upopte grahāḥ sādyante sve vā etad yonau sādyante pūrvārdhe vā ime mukhasya prāṇā etat khalu vai havirdhānasya pūrvārdhaṃ yad dakṣiṇaṃ havirdhānaṃ tasmād dakṣiṇe havirdhāne prāṇā vā eta itare grahā āyur dhruvo nava vai prāṇā āyur daśamaṃ tasmād eṣa daśamo gṛhyate daśamaṃ hy āyur rājaputro dhruvaṃ gopāyati sarvāsāṃ vā etat prajānām āyur gopāyati tasmād rājaputro vīryavattamo yady abhicareta || idam aham amuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasyāyuḥ pravartayāmi || iti dhruvaṃ pravartayed āyur evāsya pravartayati yat pravartayet sarvāsāṃ prajānām āyuḥ pravartayec chuk prajā ṛched avartir yajamānaṃ gṛhṇīyāt kṣodhuko 'dhvaryuḥ syāt tad vyaṅgya eva || dhruvaṃ tvā dhruvakṣitim amum āsthānāc cyāvayāmi || ity āsthānād evainaṃ cyāvayati pramāyuko bhavati dhruvaṃ vai pracyavamānaṃ viśvā bhūtānu pracyavante pra yajamāna āsthānāc cyavate tad abhimṛśyo divi divyān dṛṃhāntarikṣe antarikṣyān pṛthivyāṃ pārthivān iti yathāsthāma vā etat prajā dṛṃhati sva āyatane yajamānam āyuṣā vā eṣa vīryeṇa vyṛdhyate yasya dhruvaḥ skandaty āyur vīryaṃ dhruvas tad abhimṛśyaḥ || āyurdhā asi dhruvāyur me dhehi || ity āyur evāsmin dadhāti varo dakṣiṇā vareṇaiva varaṃ spṛṇoty ātmā hi varaḥ putrasenasya ha vai bhaimasene dhruva upadadāsa taṃ śṛṇvānaḥ sthairabrahmaṇa ṛtenaibhyo lokebhya āpyāyayāṃcakāra || svāhā diva āpyāyasva || iti sa tṛtīyaṃ babhūva || svāhāntarikṣād āpyāyasva || iti sa dvibhāgaṃ babhūva || svāhā pṛthivyā āpyāyasva || iti sa pupūre tad ṛtenaivaibhyo lokebhyo dhruva āpyāyayitavyo dvādaśe stotre 'vanayati || dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaro yajño yajñaḥ prajāpatiḥ prājāpatyaḥ puruṣo yāvān eva puruṣas tasminn āyur dadhāti yat stūyamāne 'vanayed garbhāḥ prapādukāḥ syur yañ śasyamāne yuvānaḥ pramīyeran yañ śaste bahiḥ prāṇān dadhyāt sakṛñ śastāyāṃ madhyato 'vanīyo madhyato vā etat prajānām āyur dadhāti || svayaṃbhūr asi śreṣṭho raśmiḥ priyo devānāṃ saṃsadanīyaḥ || taṃ tvā subhava devā abhisaṃviśantu || āyurdhā asi dhruvāyur me dhehi || ity āyur evāsmin dadhāti || varcodhā asi dhruva varco me dhehi || viśvadarśata evam ahaṃ viśvadarśato bhūyāsam || iti viśvadarśato ha bhavaty asau vā ādityaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ śreṣṭho raśmir yathaiṣa svayam abhavad evaṃ svayaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
4.6.6.d: आयुर् वै ध्रुवस् तम् उत्तमं गृह्णात्य् उत्तमं ह्य् आयुः स्थाल्या गृह्णात्य् आयुषो धृत्यै पूर्णं गृह्णाति सर्वम् आयुर् एति प्राणो वै गायत्र्य् आयुर् ध्रुवो यद् एष आ तृतीयात् सवनात् परिशये तस्माद् यावद् आयुस् तावान् प्राण आयुर् वै ध्रुवो यद् अग्निष्टोमम् आस्त आयुर् एवाप्त्वा निःसर्पत्य् आयुर् वै ध्रुवो यत् केवलं जुहुयाद् आयुः प्रजानां प्रदध्यात् परिधानीयायां शस्यमानायाम् अवनयति स ह्य् अन्तो होतुश् चमसे ऽवनयति वैश्वदेवो वै होता वैश्वदेवीर् इमाः प्रजाः सर्वासु वा एतत् प्रजास्व् आयुर् दधाति जनानाम् इत्य् आहुः सर्वासां वा एतत् प्रजानाम् आयुः सर्वाभ्यः प्रजाभ्यो गृह्यत उभयतोवैश्वानरो गृह्यत उभयतोवैश्वानरो ह्य् अयं प्राणो ऽयं वाव वैश्वानरो यो ऽयम् अवाङ् प्राणो यद् एष केवला उत्तरे हविर्धाने साद्यते तस्माद् एषो ऽर्धभाक् प्राणानाम् अर्धभाजा इतरे हिरण्ये ऽधि सादयेद् आयुःकामस्यामृतं वै हिरण्यम् आयुर् ध्रुवो ऽमृत एवास्यायुर् दधात्य् उपोप्ते ऽन्ये ग्रहाः साद्यन्ते ऽनुपोप्ते ध्रुवस् तस्माद् अस्थ्नान्ये पशवः प्रतितिष्ठन्ति मांसेन पुरुषः प्राणा वा उपरवा यद् एत उपोप्ते ग्रहाः साद्यन्ते स्वे वा एतद् योनौ साद्यन्ते पूर्वार्धे वा इमे मुखस्य प्राणा एतत् खलु वै हविर्धानस्य पूर्वार्धं यद् दक्षिणं हविर्धानं तस्माद् दक्षिणे हविर्धाने प्राणा वा एत इतरे ग्रहा आयुर् ध्रुवो नव वै प्राणा आयुर् दशमं तस्माद् एष दशमो गृह्यते दशमं ह्य् आयुर् राजपुत्रो ध्रुवं गोपायति सर्वासां वा एतत् प्रजानाम् आयुर् गोपायति तस्माद् राजपुत्रो वीर्यवत्तमो यद्य् अभिचरेत ॥ इदम् अहम् अमुष्यामुष्यायणस्यायुः प्रवर्तयामि ॥ इति ध्रुवं प्रवर्तयेद् आयुर् एवास्य प्रवर्तयति यत् प्रवर्तयेत् सर्वासां प्रजानाम् आयुः प्रवर्तयेच् छुक् प्रजा ऋछेद् अवर्तिर् यजमानं गृह्णीयात् क्षोधुको ऽध्वर्युः स्यात् तद् व्यङ्ग्य एव ॥ ध्रुवं त्वा ध्रुवक्षितिम् अमुम् आस्थानाच् च्यावयामि ॥ इत्य् आस्थानाद् एवैनं च्यावयति प्रमायुको भवति ध्रुवं वै प्रच्यवमानं विश्वा भूतानु प्रच्यवन्ते प्र यजमान आस्थानाच् च्यवते तद् अभिमृश्यो दिवि दिव्यान् दृंहान्तरिक्षे अन्तरिक्ष्यान् पृथिव्यां पार्थिवान् इति यथास्थाम वा एतत् प्रजा दृंहति स्व आयतने यजमानम् आयुषा वा एष वीर्येण व्यृध्यते यस्य ध्रुवः स्कन्दत्य् आयुर् वीर्यं ध्रुवस् तद् अभिमृश्यः ॥ आयुर्धा असि ध्रुवायुर् मे धेहि ॥ इत्य् आयुर् एवास्मिन् दधाति वरो दक्षिणा वरेणैव वरं स्पृणोत्य् आत्मा हि वरः पुत्रसेनस्य ह वै भैमसेने ध्रुव उपददास तं शृण्वानः स्थैरब्रह्मण ऋतेनैभ्यो लोकेभ्य आप्याययांचकार ॥ स्वाहा दिव आप्यायस्व ॥ इति स तृतीयं बभूव ॥ स्वाहान्तरिक्षाद् आप्यायस्व ॥ इति स द्विभागं बभूव ॥ स्वाहा पृथिव्या आप्यायस्व ॥ इति स पुपूरे तद् ऋतेनैवैभ्यो लोकेभ्यो ध्रुव आप्याययितव्यो द्वादशे स्तोत्रे ऽवनयति ॥ द्वादश मासाः संवत्सरः संवत्सरो यज्ञो यज्ञः प्रजापतिः प्राजापत्यः पुरुषो यावान् एव पुरुषस् तस्मिन्न् आयुर् दधाति यत् स्तूयमाने ऽवनयेद् गर्भाः प्रपादुकाः स्युर् यञ् शस्यमाने युवानः प्रमीयेरन् यञ् शस्ते बहिः प्राणान् दध्यात् सकृञ् शस्तायां मध्यतो ऽवनीयो मध्यतो वा एतत् प्रजानाम् आयुर् दधाति ॥ स्वयंभूर् असि श्रेष्ठो रश्मिः प्रियो देवानां संसदनीयः ॥ तं त्वा सुभव देवा अभिसंविशन्तु ॥ आयुर्धा असि ध्रुवायुर् मे धेहि ॥ इत्य् आयुर् एवास्मिन् दधाति ॥ वर्चोधा असि ध्रुव वर्चो मे धेहि ॥ इति वर्च एवास्मिन् दधाति ॥ इषो ऽसि त्वेषो ऽसि नृम्णो ऽसि व्रतो ऽसि दक्षो ऽसि तस्य त इषस्य त्वेषस्य नृम्णस्य व्रतस्य दक्षस्य भक्षीय स्वस्य चारणस्य च शूद्रस्य चार्यस्य च यथा त्वं सूर्यासि विश्वदर्शत एवम् अहं विश्वदर्शतो भूयासम् ॥ इति विश्वदर्शतो ह भवत्य् असौ वा आदित्यः स्वयंभूः श्रेष्ठो रश्मिर् यथैष स्वयम् अभवद् एवं स्वयं भवति य एवं वेद ॥
4.6.6.m:
The Dhruva [cup], indeed, is life.
He draws it last.
For life is last.
He draws [it] with an earthen vessel,
for the retention of life.
He draws [it] full;
he attains a full lifespan.
The Gāyatrī, indeed, is breath.
The Dhruva is life.
Because this [cup] lies beside [the fire] until the third pressing,
therefore as great as life is, so great is breath.
The Dhruva, indeed, is life.
In that he remains until the Agniṣṭoma,
having obtained life, he creeps out.
The Dhruva, indeed, is life.
If he were to offer it alone, he would hand over the life of creatures [to destruction].
While the concluding verse is being recited, he pours it out [into the Hotṛ's cup];
for that is the end.
He pours it out into the Hotṛ's cup.
The Hotṛ, indeed, belongs to all the gods;
these creatures belong to all the gods.
He thereby places life in all creatures.
'Of people,' they say;
this life of all creatures is indeed drawn for all creatures.
It is drawn with Vaiśvānara on both sides;
for this breath has Vaiśvānara on both sides.
This downward breath, indeed, is Vaiśvānara.
Because this [cup] is placed alone on the northern Havirdhāna cart,
therefore this one shares half of the breaths; the others share [the other] half.
He should place it upon gold for one who desires life.
Gold, indeed, is immortality;
the Dhruva is life.
He thereby places life in immortality for him.
The other cups are placed on [earth] that is heaped up; the Dhruva on [earth] that is not heaped up.
Therefore other animals stand firm by bone; man by flesh.
The Uparavas, indeed, are the breaths.
When these cups are placed on [earth] that is heaped up,
they are placed in their own womb.
These breaths of the mouth are in the front part.
That southern Havirdhāna cart is indeed the front part of the Havirdhāna [shed].
Therefore [they are placed] on the southern Havirdhāna cart.
These other cups are the breaths;
the Dhruva is life.
Nine, indeed, are the breaths;
life is the tenth.
Therefore this tenth [cup] is drawn;
for life is the tenth.
A king's son guards the Dhruva.
He thereby guards the life of all creatures.
Therefore a king's son is most heroic.
If he should practice sorcery:
'Here do I roll away the life of so-and-so, son of so-and-so'—with these words he should roll away the Dhruva.
He thereby rolls away his life.
If he were to roll it away, he would roll away the life of all creatures;
sorrow would come upon creatures;
misfortune would seize the sacrificer;
the Adhvaryu would become hungry.
Therefore it should be just subtly indicated [by movement]:
'Firm thee, of firm dwelling, do I dislodge so-and-so from his place,' [he says].
He dislodges him from his place;
he becomes liable to die.
When the Dhruva falls down, indeed, all beings fall down after it;
the sacrificer falls away from his place.
Then it is to be touched:
'In heaven establish those belonging to heaven, in the intermediate space those belonging to the intermediate space, on earth those belonging to earth.'
He thereby establishes creatures according to their places,
and the sacrificer in his own domain.
He indeed is deprived of life, of virility, whose Dhruva is spilt;
the Dhruva is life and virility.
Then it is to be touched:
'Life-giver art thou, O Dhruva;
bestow life on me.'
He thereby places life in him.
A choice gift is the dakṣiṇā;
with a choice gift he saves the choice [thing];
for the self is the choice [thing].
The Dhruva of Putrasena Bhaimaseni ran dry.
Śṛṇvāna Sthairabrahmaṇa made it swell from these worlds by means of the truth:
'Svāhā, swell from heaven!' [he said];
it became a third [full].
'Svāhā, swell from the intermediate space!' [he said];
it became two-thirds [full].
'Svāhā, swell from earth!' [he said];
it was filled.
Therefore the Dhruva is to be made to swell from these worlds by means of the truth.
He pours it out at the twelfth stotra.
Twelve months are the year;
the year is the sacrifice;
the sacrifice is Prajāpati;
man belongs to Prajāpati.
As great as man is, in him he places life.
If he were to pour it out while [the stotra] is being chanted, embryos would be liable to fall [prematurely].
If while [the śastra] is being recited, young men would die.
If when it has been recited, he would place the breaths outside.
Once it has been recited, it is to be poured out in the middle.
He thereby places life in the middle of creatures:
'Self-existent art thou, the best ray, dear to the gods, fit for sitting together;
as such, O fortunate one, let the gods enter into thee.
Life-giver art thou, O Dhruva;
bestow life on me,'
[with these words];
he thereby places life in him.
'Splendour-giver art thou, O Dhruva;
bestow splendour on me,'
[with these words];
he thereby places splendour in him.
'Food art thou,
energy art thou,
manly power art thou,
vow art thou,
skill art thou;
of that food, energy, manly power, vow, skill of thine may I partake,
both of my own [people] and of a stranger, both of Śūdra and of Ārya;
as thou, O Sūrya, art visible to all, so may I become visible to all,'
[with these words];
he indeed becomes visible to all.
Yonder sun, indeed, is the self-existent, the best ray;
as he came to be of himself, so does he who knows thus come to be of himself.

4.6.7.s: athaita ṛtugrahāḥ saṃvatsarasya vā ete vidhṛtyai gṛhyante dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaras tasmād dvādaśa ṛtugrahā madhuś ca mādhavaś ca vāsantikā ṛtū asannā hūyante 'sannā hīma ṛtavo nānyo'nyam abhiprapadyate yad anyo'nyam abhiprapadyeta ṛtā ṛtur abhīyād atha yad anyo'nyaḥ prapadyate tasmād idam ṛtā ṛtur anunihitāḥ pariplavanta ubhayatomukham ṛtupātram ubhayatomukhā hīma ṛtavo na vai tad vidma yata ṛtūnāṃ mukhaṃ saha prathamaṃ gṛhṇāte sahottamaṃ saha yujyete saha vimucyete caturdaśa vā etat kuruto 'ti vā etad recayato 'sti māsas trayodaśas tam evaitenāptvāvarunddha ṛtubhyo vai prajāḥ prajāyante yat ṣaḍ ṛtunā catur ṛtubhir ṛtubhyo vāvāsmā etac catuṣpadaḥ paśūn prajanayato 'tha yac catur ṛtubhir dvir ṛtunartubhyo vāvāsmā etad dvipadaḥ paśūn prajanayato yad dvir ṛtunā dvau hīmā ṛtū atha yad dve ṛtupātre dvaudvau hīma ṛtavo nānuyajati vaiśvānaro vaṣaṭkāro yad anuyajed vaiśvānaram ṛtuṣv anvavasṛjed andho vā idam āsīd avyāvṛttam ahar āsīn na rātris tad devā ṛtugrahair vyāvartayan yad ṛtugrahā gṛhyante 'horātrayor vyāvṛttyai saṃvatsaro vai svargo lokas tasya vā eta ākramā yad ṛtugrahā yad ṛtugrahā gṛhyante svargasya lokasyākrāntyai ||
4.6.7.d: अथैत ऋतुग्रहाः संवत्सरस्य वा एते विधृत्यै गृह्यन्ते द्वादश मासाः संवत्सरस् तस्माद् द्वादश ऋतुग्रहा मधुश् च माधवश् च वासन्तिका ऋतू असन्ना हूयन्ते ऽसन्ना हीम ऋतवो नान्योऽन्यम् अभिप्रपद्यते यद् अन्योऽन्यम् अभिप्रपद्येत ऋता ऋतुर् अभीयाद् अथ यद् अन्योऽन्यः प्रपद्यते तस्माद् इदम् ऋता ऋतुर् अनुनिहिताः परिप्लवन्त उभयतोमुखम् ऋतुपात्रम् उभयतोमुखा हीम ऋतवो न वै तद् विद्म यत ऋतूनां मुखं सह प्रथमं गृह्णाते सहोत्तमं सह युज्येते सह विमुच्येते चतुर्दश वा एतत् कुरुतो ऽति वा एतद् रेचयतो ऽस्ति मासस् त्रयोदशस् तम् एवैतेनाप्त्वावरुन्द्ध ऋतुभ्यो वै प्रजाः प्रजायन्ते यत् षड् ऋतुना चतुर् ऋतुभिर् ऋतुभ्यो वावास्मा एतच् चतुष्पदः पशून् प्रजनयतो ऽथ यच् चतुर् ऋतुभिर् द्विर् ऋतुनर्तुभ्यो वावास्मा एतद् द्विपदः पशून् प्रजनयतो यद् द्विर् ऋतुना द्वौ हीमा ऋतू अथ यद् द्वे ऋतुपात्रे द्वौद्वौ हीम ऋतवो नानुयजति वैश्वानरो वषट्कारो यद् अनुयजेद् वैश्वानरम् ऋतुष्व् अन्ववसृजेद् अन्धो वा इदम् आसीद् अव्यावृत्तम् अहर् आसीन् न रात्रिस् तद् देवा ऋतुग्रहैर् व्यावर्तयन् यद् ऋतुग्रहा गृह्यन्ते ऽहोरात्रयोर् व्यावृत्त्यै संवत्सरो वै स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्य वा एत आक्रमा यद् ऋतुग्रहा यद् ऋतुग्रहा गृह्यन्ते स्वर्गस्य लोकस्याक्रान्त्यै ॥
4.6.7.m:
Now these Ṛtu cups:
these are indeed drawn for the support of the year.
Twelve months are the year;
therefore there are twelve Ṛtu cups.
Madhu and Mādhava are the two spring seasons.
They are offered without being deposited [on the khara];
for these seasons are not seated.
One does not enter into the other.
If one were to enter into the other, season would cross over season.
Now because one succeeds the other,
therefore these seasons, arranged in sequence, revolve.
The vessel for the seasons has openings on both sides;
for these seasons have openings on both sides.
We do not know whence the opening of the seasons [begins].
Together they draw the first, together the last.
Together they are yoked, together they are unyoked.
They thereby make fourteen;
they thereby make an excess.
There is a thirteenth month;
having reached it by this, he secures it.
From the seasons, indeed, creatures are born.
When six [times he offers] with 'By the season' [and] four with 'By the seasons',
they two thereby generate four-footed cattle from the seasons for him.
Now when four [times he offers] with 'By the seasons' [and] twice with 'By the season',
they two thereby generate two-footed cattle from the seasons for him.
In that [he offers] twice with 'By the season'—
for these two are two seasons.
Now in that there are two season vessels—
for these seasons are two by two.
He does not perform an after-sacrifice;
the vaṣaṭ-call is Vaiśvānara.
If he were to perform an after-sacrifice, he would unleash Vaiśvānara upon the seasons.
Blind, indeed, was this [world], undifferentiated;
it was day, not night.
The gods differentiated it with the Ṛtu cups.
When the Ṛtu cups are drawn,
[it is] for the differentiation of day and night.
The heavenly world is indeed the year;
the Ṛtu cups are the stepping-stones of it.
When the Ṛtu cups are drawn,
[it is] for stepping up to the heavenly world.

4.6.8.s: ādityā vā ita uttamāḥ svargaṃ lokam āyaṃs te vā itaḥ pratisaṃhitāḥ purastād evānyat sarvaṃ saṃvatsaro vai svargo lokaḥ saṃvatsaram etau kalpayituṃ plāyete yad adhvaryū yad aindrāgnam ṛtupātreṇa gṛhṇāti saṃvatsaraṃ vā etad anvārabhate svargāya lokāyātho jyotir upariṣṭād dadhāti svargasya lokasya samaṣṭyay asau vā ādityaḥ śukraḥ puruṣo vaiśvadevo yañ śukrapātreṇa vaiśvadevaṃ gṛhṇāti tasmāt puruṣa evāmuṃ pratyak sarve 'nye nyañcaḥ paśavo devāś ca vā asurāś cāspardhanta te devāḥ prātaḥsavane vaiśvadeve yajñaṃ saṃsthāpyam apaśyaṃs taṃ prātaḥsavane samasthāpayan yad vaiśvadevaḥ prātaḥsavane gṛhyate prātaḥsavane vā etad vaiśvadeve yajñaṃ saṃsthāpayati tena saṃsthitenāriṣṭena bhūtena pracaranti devā vai sarve prātaḥsavanam abhyāyachan nottarābhyāṃ savanābhyām atiṣṭhanta yad vaiśvadevaḥ prātaḥsavane hūyate prātaḥsavane vā etad vaiśvadeve devatās tarpayanti tās tṛptā uttare savane abhisṛjyamānā yanti vajro vai marutvatīyā vajra eva prathamo 'pagūrtir dvitīyaḥ stṛtir uttamo vajro vai dhanur dhanur eva prathamaḥ pratihitir dvitīyo visṛṣṭas tṛtīyaś cakriyau vā ete yajñasya yan marutvatīyā akṣo madhyamaḥ pakṣasī abhito marudbhir vai vīryeṇendro vṛtram ahan na ṛte marudbhyo 'śaknod vīryaṃ kartuṃ yan marutvatīyo graho gṛhyate marutvatīyaṃ śasyate tena mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ vīryavat kathaṃ savanāny ṛtumanti vettheti pṛched ṛtugrahaiḥ prātaḥsavanam ṛtuman marutvatīyair mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ sāvitreṇa tṛtīyasavanaṃ marutvatīyayoḥ sannayor dakṣiṇā dīyante sve vā etad yonau dakṣiṇā dīyante paridhayo vā ete yajñasya yan marutvatīyās tasmān marutvatīyān dakṣiṇā nātidīyante yad atidadyād yathā bahiṣparidhi skannam evaṃ syād yadi kāmayeta viḍ ojīyasī syād abalīyaḥ kṣatram iti yasyā marutvatīyaḥ pūrvo 'rdhaṛcas tāṃ purorucaṃ kuryād viśaṃ vā etad ojīyasīm akar abalīyaḥ kṣatraṃ yadi kāmayeta kṣatram ojīyaḥ syād abalīyasī viḍ iti yasyā aindraḥ pūrvo 'rdhaṛcas tāṃ purorucaṃ kuryāt kṣatraṃ vā etad ojīyo 'kar abalīyasīṃ viśaṃ jāmi vā etad yajñe kriyate yan marutvatīyo graho gṛhyate marutvatīyaṃ śasyate paśavo vai maruto 'jāmi paśavas tena tad ajāmy ṛtupātram ālabhya pratigṛhṇāty ṛtavo vai marutaḥ saṃvatsara ṛtava āyuḥ saṃvatsara āyuṣi vā etad adhvaryuḥ śrayate vṛtraṃ vā eṣa hanti yo marutvatīyān grahān gṛhṇīte māhendre sarve kāmāḥ sarvān vā etat kāmān āpnoti sarvān vyaśnotīndro vai vṛtram ahan so 'nyān devān atyamanyata sa mahendro 'bhavat sa etam uddhāram udaharata vṛtraṃ hatvā tad uddhāra evāsyaiṣa bhāga eva tasmād rājā saṃgrāmaṃ jitvodājam udajate śukrapātreṇa māhendraṃ gṛhṇāti vadanti grāvāṇo vadanty aulūkhalā manthanty āśiram indre vā etad agrā āgate ghoṣam akurvatātho yajamāna eva tejo dadhati ||
4.6.8.d: आदित्या वा इत उत्तमाः स्वर्गं लोकम् आयंस् ते वा इतः प्रतिसंहिताः पुरस्ताद् एवान्यत् सर्वं संवत्सरो वै स्वर्गो लोकः संवत्सरम् एतौ कल्पयितुं प्लायेते यद् अध्वर्यू यद् ऐन्द्राग्नम् ऋतुपात्रेण गृह्णाति संवत्सरं वा एतद् अन्वारभते स्वर्गाय लोकायाथो ज्योतिर् उपरिष्टाद् दधाति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यय् असौ वा आदित्यः शुक्रः पुरुषो वैश्वदेवो यञ् शुक्रपात्रेण वैश्वदेवं गृह्णाति तस्मात् पुरुष एवामुं प्रत्यक् सर्वे ऽन्ये न्यञ्चः पशवो देवाश् च वा असुराश् चास्पर्धन्त ते देवाः प्रातःसवने वैश्वदेवे यज्ञं संस्थाप्यम् अपश्यंस् तं प्रातःसवने समस्थापयन् यद् वैश्वदेवः प्रातःसवने गृह्यते प्रातःसवने वा एतद् वैश्वदेवे यज्ञं संस्थापयति तेन संस्थितेनारिष्टेन भूतेन प्रचरन्ति देवा वै सर्वे प्रातःसवनम् अभ्यायछन् नोत्तराभ्यां सवनाभ्याम् अतिष्ठन्त यद् वैश्वदेवः प्रातःसवने हूयते प्रातःसवने वा एतद् वैश्वदेवे देवतास् तर्पयन्ति तास् तृप्ता उत्तरे सवने अभिसृज्यमाना यन्ति वज्रो वै मरुत्वतीया वज्र एव प्रथमो ऽपगूर्तिर् द्वितीयः स्तृतिर् उत्तमो वज्रो वै धनुर् धनुर् एव प्रथमः प्रतिहितिर् द्वितीयो विसृष्टस् तृतीयश् चक्रियौ वा एते यज्ञस्य यन् मरुत्वतीया अक्षो मध्यमः पक्षसी अभितो मरुद्भिर् वै वीर्येणेन्द्रो वृत्रम् अहन् न ऋते मरुद्भ्यो ऽशक्नोद् वीर्यं कर्तुं यन् मरुत्वतीयो ग्रहो गृह्यते मरुत्वतीयं शस्यते तेन माध्यंदिनं सवनं वीर्यवत् कथं सवनान्य् ऋतुमन्ति वेत्थेति पृछेद् ऋतुग्रहैः प्रातःसवनम् ऋतुमन् मरुत्वतीयैर् माध्यंदिनं सवनं सावित्रेण तृतीयसवनं मरुत्वतीययोः सन्नयोर् दक्षिणा दीयन्ते स्वे वा एतद् योनौ दक्षिणा दीयन्ते परिधयो वा एते यज्ञस्य यन् मरुत्वतीयास् तस्मान् मरुत्वतीयान् दक्षिणा नातिदीयन्ते यद् अतिदद्याद् यथा बहिष्परिधि स्कन्नम् एवं स्याद् यदि कामयेत विड् ओजीयसी स्याद् अबलीयः क्षत्रम् इति यस्या मरुत्वतीयः पूर्वो ऽर्धऋचस् तां पुरोरुचं कुर्याद् विशं वा एतद् ओजीयसीम् अकर् अबलीयः क्षत्रं यदि कामयेत क्षत्रम् ओजीयः स्याद् अबलीयसी विड् इति यस्या ऐन्द्रः पूर्वो ऽर्धऋचस् तां पुरोरुचं कुर्यात् क्षत्रं वा एतद् ओजीयो ऽकर् अबलीयसीं विशं जामि वा एतद् यज्ञे क्रियते यन् मरुत्वतीयो ग्रहो गृह्यते मरुत्वतीयं शस्यते पशवो वै मरुतो ऽजामि पशवस् तेन तद् अजाम्य् ऋतुपात्रम् आलभ्य प्रतिगृह्णात्य् ऋतवो वै मरुतः संवत्सर ऋतव आयुः संवत्सर आयुषि वा एतद् अध्वर्युः श्रयते वृत्रं वा एष हन्ति यो मरुत्वतीयान् ग्रहान् गृह्णीते माहेन्द्रे सर्वे कामाः सर्वान् वा एतत् कामान् आप्नोति सर्वान् व्यश्नोतीन्द्रो वै वृत्रम् अहन् सो ऽन्यान् देवान् अत्यमन्यत स महेन्द्रो ऽभवत् स एतम् उद्धारम् उदहरत वृत्रं हत्वा तद् उद्धार एवास्यैष भाग एव तस्माद् राजा संग्रामं जित्वोदाजम् उदजते शुक्रपात्रेण माहेन्द्रं गृह्णाति वदन्ति ग्रावाणो वदन्त्य् औलूखला मन्थन्त्य् आशिरम् इन्द्रे वा एतद् अग्रा आगते घोषम् अकुर्वताथो यजमान एव तेजो दधति ॥
4.6.8.m:
The Ādityas, indeed, went from here as the last to the heavenly world.
They were firmly set from here, while everything else was beforehand.
The heavenly world is indeed the year.
The two Adhvaryus run to arrange the year.
In that he draws the Aindrāgna cup with the season vessel,
he thereby takes hold of the year for the heavenly world.
Moreover, he places a light on top,
for the attainment of the heavenly world.
Yonder sun is Śukra;
man is Vaiśvadeva.
In that he draws the Vaiśvadeva cup with the Śukra vessel,
therefore man alone faces yonder [sun],
while all other cattle face downward.
The gods and the Asuras contended.
The gods saw that the sacrifice was to be concluded at the morning pressing with the Vaiśvadeva cup.
They concluded it at the morning pressing.
In that the Vaiśvadeva cup is drawn at the morning pressing,
he thereby concludes the sacrifice at the morning pressing with the Vaiśvadeva cup.
With that concluded, uninjured, brought into being, they proceed.
All the gods, indeed, approached the morning pressing;
they did not remain for the two later pressings.
In that the Vaiśvadeva cup is offered at the morning pressing,
they thereby gratify the deities at the morning pressing with the Vaiśvadeva cup.
Gratified, they go, being joined with the two later pressings.
The Marutvatīya cups are indeed a thunderbolt.
The first is indeed a thunderbolt;
the second is raising [it];
the last is striking down.
The bow is indeed a thunderbolt;
the first is indeed the bow;
the second is fixing [the arrow];
the third is releasing [it].
The Marutvatīya cups are indeed the two wheels of the sacrifice;
the middle is the axle;
the two side-frames are on both sides.
With the Maruts, by virility, Indra slew Vṛtra.
Without the Maruts he could not display virility.
In that the Marutvatīya cup is drawn and the Marutvatīya hymn is recited,
thereby the midday pressing is full of virility.
He should ask: 'How do you know the pressings to have seasons?'
The morning pressing has seasons through the Ṛtu cups;
the midday pressing through the Marutvatīya cups;
the third pressing through the Sāvitra cup.
When the two Marutvatīya cups are deposited, the sacrificial gifts are given;
they are given in their own womb.
The Marutvatīya cups are the enclosing sticks of the sacrifice;
therefore the sacrificial gifts are not given beyond the Marutvatīya cups.
If he were to give them beyond, it would be just as if spilled outside the enclosing sticks.
If he should desire: 'May the commonalty be stronger, the nobility weaker,' he should make that verse whose prior half-verse belongs to the Maruts into the puroruc.
He thereby makes the commonalty stronger, the nobility weaker.
If he should desire: 'May the nobility be stronger, the commonalty weaker,' he should make that verse whose prior half-verse belongs to Indra into the puroruc.
He thereby makes the nobility stronger, the commonalty weaker.
A redundancy is indeed committed in the sacrifice in that the Marutvatīya cup is drawn and the Marutvatīya hymn is recited.
The Maruts are cattle;
cattle are not redundant;
thereby it is not redundant. Having touched the season vessel, he takes it.
The Maruts are seasons;
the seasons are the year;
the year is life.
The Adhvaryu thereby leans upon life.
He who draws the Marutvatīya cups slays Vṛtra.
All desires are in the Māhendra cup;
he thereby attains all desires, he obtains all desires.
Indra slew Vṛtra;
he thought himself superior to the other gods.
He became the Great Indra (Mahendra).
Having slain Vṛtra, he took this chosen portion for himself.
Therefore it is a chosen portion.
This is his portion alone.
Therefore a king, having won a battle, drives off the prize of victory.
With the Śukra vessel he draws the Māhendra cup.
The pressing-stones sound;
the mortars sound;
they churn the milk mixture.
When Indra came to the forefront, they made a sound.
Moreover, they place splendor in the sacrificer.

4.6.9.s: etad vā eṣābhyanūktā || aṣṭau putrāso aditer ye jātās tanvas pari | devaṃ upa prait saptabhiḥ parā mārtāṇḍam āsyat || ity eṣa vāva sa upāṃśusavano grāvā tasya vā eṣa somapītho yad ādityaṃ mekṣayanti || vivasvann ādityaiṣa te somapīthaḥ || iti somapīthenaivainaṃ samardhayati vyāno vā upāṃśusavanaḥ prajā ādityo vyānaṃ vā etat prajāsu dadhāti paśavo vā ādityo yad dadhnā madhyataḥ śrīṇāti madhyato vā etat paśūnāṃ payo dadhāty atha yat taptātaṅkyaṃ tasmād āmā satī pakvaṃ duhe yadi kāmayeta varṣet parjanyā iti || yā divyā vṛṣṭis tayā tvā śrīṇāmi || iti dadhnopariṣṭād ādityaṃ śrīṇīyāt paśavo vā ādityaḥ paśubhya eṣo 'muto varṣati paśūn eva vṛṣṭyābhijigharti yadi kāmayeta garbhāḥ śrīvyeyur ity udgṛhyādityam avekṣeta garbhā ha śrevukā bhavanti śukravatī vai pūrve savane aśukraṃ tṛtīyaṃ savanaṃ yad dvidevatyānāṃ saṃsravān avanayaty āgrāyaṇam abhipraskandayati tena tṛtīyasavanaṃ śukravad devā asurān hatvā mṛtyor abibhayus te nāthaiṣiṇo nyañcanaiṣiṇa etā devatā bhūyiṣṭhāḥ prāviśan yad dvidevatyāṃs tasmād dvidevatyebhya ādityo nirgṛhyate bṛhatībhyāṃ gṛhṇāti paśavo vai bṛhatīḥ prajā āditya etāvāṃl loko yāvad uddhataṃ yat saṃprasārayitvā gṛhṇāti lokaṃ vā etad annādyaṃ yajamāno bhrātṛvyasya vṛṅkte 'tho imā eva prajā annādyāyāvarunddhe yady asya bhrātṛvyo yajeta bahirvedi tiṣṭhet tathā hainaṃ nāvarunddhe paśavo vā ādityo 'gnī rudro 'gner etās tanvo yad dhiṣṇyā yat saṃprasārayitvā gṛhṇāti rudrād vā etat paśūn antardadhāty apidhāyopa niṣkrāmati paśūnāṃ gopīthāyādityo vai dvidevatyānām anuyājas tasmāt tān nānuyajati dvidevatyā vā ādityasya prayājās tasmāt tān nānuyajati paśavo vā ādityo 'gnī rudro brāhmaṇa upadraṣṭā yad īkṣamāṇo juhuyāt pradhīyamānānām eṣām upadraṣṭā syād anyatrekṣamāṇena hotavyam anupadraṣṭaiṣāṃ bhavati ||
4.6.9.d: एतद् वा एषाभ्यनूक्ता ॥ अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेर् ये जातास् तन्वस् परि । देवं उप प्रैत् सप्तभिः परा मार्ताण्डम् आस्यत् ॥ इत्य् एष वाव स उपांशुसवनो ग्रावा तस्य वा एष सोमपीथो यद् आदित्यं मेक्षयन्ति ॥ विवस्वन्न् आदित्यैष ते सोमपीथः ॥ इति सोमपीथेनैवैनं समर्धयति व्यानो वा उपांशुसवनः प्रजा आदित्यो व्यानं वा एतत् प्रजासु दधाति पशवो वा आदित्यो यद् दध्ना मध्यतः श्रीणाति मध्यतो वा एतत् पशूनां पयो दधात्य् अथ यत् तप्तातङ्क्यं तस्माद् आमा सती पक्वं दुहे यदि कामयेत वर्षेत् पर्जन्या इति ॥ या दिव्या वृष्टिस् तया त्वा श्रीणामि ॥ इति दध्नोपरिष्टाद् आदित्यं श्रीणीयात् पशवो वा आदित्यः पशुभ्य एषो ऽमुतो वर्षति पशून् एव वृष्ट्याभिजिघर्ति यदि कामयेत गर्भाः श्रीव्येयुर् इत्य् उद्गृह्यादित्यम् अवेक्षेत गर्भा ह श्रेवुका भवन्ति शुक्रवती वै पूर्वे सवने अशुक्रं तृतीयं सवनं यद् द्विदेवत्यानां संस्रवान् अवनयत्य् आग्रायणम् अभिप्रस्कन्दयति तेन तृतीयसवनं शुक्रवद् देवा असुरान् हत्वा मृत्योर् अबिभयुस् ते नाथैषिणो न्यञ्चनैषिण एता देवता भूयिष्ठाः प्राविशन् यद् द्विदेवत्यांस् तस्माद् द्विदेवत्येभ्य आदित्यो निर्गृह्यते बृहतीभ्यां गृह्णाति पशवो वै बृहतीः प्रजा आदित्य एतावांल् लोको यावद् उद्धतं यत् संप्रसारयित्वा गृह्णाति लोकं वा एतद् अन्नाद्यं यजमानो भ्रातृव्यस्य वृङ्क्ते ऽथो इमा एव प्रजा अन्नाद्यायावरुन्द्धे यद्य् अस्य भ्रातृव्यो यजेत बहिर्वेदि तिष्ठेत् तथा हैनं नावरुन्द्धे पशवो वा आदित्यो ऽग्नी रुद्रो ऽग्नेर् एतास् तन्वो यद् धिष्ण्या यत् संप्रसारयित्वा गृह्णाति रुद्राद् वा एतत् पशून् अन्तर्दधात्य् अपिधायोप निष्क्रामति पशूनां गोपीथायादित्यो वै द्विदेवत्यानाम् अनुयाजस् तस्मात् तान् नानुयजति द्विदेवत्या वा आदित्यस्य प्रयाजास् तस्मात् तान् नानुयजति पशवो वा आदित्यो ऽग्नी रुद्रो ब्राह्मण उपद्रष्टा यद् ईक्षमाणो जुहुयात् प्रधीयमानानाम् एषाम् उपद्रष्टा स्याद् अन्यत्रेक्षमाणेन होतव्यम् अनुपद्रष्टैषां भवति ॥
4.6.9.m:
Regarding this, indeed, it has been recited:
“Eight are the sons of Aditi who were born from her body; / with seven she approached the gods; Mārtāṇḍa she cast away.”
This [stone], indeed, is that Upāṃśusavana pressing-stone.
His Soma-drink, indeed, is that which they stir into the Āditya [cup]:
“O Vivasvat, O Āditya, this is your Soma-drink,” [he says];
with the Soma-drink he thus provides him.
The Upāṃśusavana, indeed, is the vyāna [breath];
the Āditya is creatures.
He thus places the vyāna in creatures.
The Āditya, indeed, is cattle.
In that he mixes [it] in the middle with curd,
he thus places milk in the middle of cattle.
Now, in that [the curd] is curdled from warm [milk],
therefore, being raw, she yields cooked [milk].
If he should desire: “May Parjanya rain,” with: “With the heavenly rain I mix you,” he should mix the Āditya [cup] from above with curd.
The Āditya, indeed, is cattle;
he rains from yonder for cattle.
He besprinkles cattle with rain.
If he should desire: “May embryos miscarry,” having held up the Āditya [cup], he should look down [upon it];
the embryos indeed become liable to miscarry.
The former two pressings possess the Śukra;
the third pressing is without the Śukra.
In that he pours together the residues of the cups for two deities and causes [them] to flow over into the Āgrāyaṇa,
thereby the third pressing is provided with the Śukra.
The gods, having slain the Asuras, were afraid of death.
Seeking a refuge, seeking a shelter, they entered most into these deities,
namely into the cups for two deities.
Therefore the Āditya [cup] is drawn from the cups for two deities.
He draws with two Bṛhatī [verses].
The Bṛhatī [verses] are cattle;
the Āditya is creatures.
As great as is the excavated [part of the altar], so great is this world.
In that he draws having stretched forth [his arms],
the sacrificer thereby takes away the world and food from his rival.
Moreover, he secures these creatures for food.
If his rival should sacrifice, he should stand outside the vedi;
thus he does not secure him.
The Āditya, indeed, is cattle;
Agni is Rudra.
These dhiṣṇya hearths are the bodies of Agni.
In that he draws having stretched forth [his arms],
he thereby separates the cattle from Rudra.
Having covered [it], he steps out,
for the protection of cattle.
The Āditya is the after-offering of the cups for two deities;
therefore he does not offer after-offerings for them.
The cups for two deities are the fore-offerings of the Āditya;
therefore he does not offer after-offerings for them.
The Āditya, indeed, is cattle;
Agni is Rudra.
The Brāhmaṇa is a witness.
If he were to sacrifice looking [at them], he would be a witness of those [cattle] being destroyed.
One must sacrifice looking elsewhere;
he becomes not a witness of them.

4.7.1.s: gāyatro vai devānāṃ savitā gāyatryā eṣa loke somo gṛhyate yad āgrayaṇas tasmād āgrāyaṇāt sāvitro nirgṛhyate so 'da ā tṛtīyāt savanāt pariśaye kriyamāṇasyakriyamāṇasya prasavāyāntarikṣaṃ vā antaryāmo 'ntarikṣam imāḥ prajā yad antaryāmapātreṇa sāvitraṃ gṛhṇāti savitā vā etat prajāḥ prasuvati prajananāyāsanno hūyate 'sannā hīmāḥ prajā nelayanti nānuyajati yad anuyajet sṛṣṭiṃ prajānāṃ vichindyād atho samānapātrau hy etau somau gṛhyete tasmān nānuyajati devā vai tṛtīyasavanam udyamaṃ nāśaknuvan prātaḥsavane tarhi savitāsīt taṃ devās tṛtīyasavanam abhiparyauhaṃs tena tṛtīyasavanam udayachanta yat sāvitras tṛtīyasavane gṛhyate savitṛprasūtā vā etat tṛtīyaṃ savanam udyachante sāvitrasya saṃsrave vaiśvadevam abhigṛhṇāti vaiśvadevīr imāḥ prajāḥ savitṛprasūtāḥ khalu vai prajāḥ prajāyante mano vai savitā vaiśvadevīr imāḥ prajāḥ sarvāsu vā etat prajāsu mano dadhāty āśīrmataḥ savanasya gṛhṇāti vaiśvadevatvāya suśarmāsi supratiṣṭhāna iti yat svit somaḥ some pratitiṣṭhati bṛhadukṣe namā iti yad bṛhad iti tena devebhyo yan namā iti tena pitṛbhya ukthabhājo vai pitaro 'stomabhāja ukthāyaiṣa gṛhyate na stotrāya yatra gṛhyate tañ śasyate sva āyatatne ||
4.7.1.d: गायत्रो वै देवानां सविता गायत्र्या एष लोके सोमो गृह्यते यद् आग्रयणस् तस्माद् आग्रायणात् सावित्रो निर्गृह्यते सो ऽद आ तृतीयात् सवनात् परिशये क्रियमाणस्यक्रियमाणस्य प्रसवायान्तरिक्षं वा अन्तर्यामो ऽन्तरिक्षम् इमाः प्रजा यद् अन्तर्यामपात्रेण सावित्रं गृह्णाति सविता वा एतत् प्रजाः प्रसुवति प्रजननायासन्नो हूयते ऽसन्ना हीमाः प्रजा नेलयन्ति नानुयजति यद् अनुयजेत् सृष्टिं प्रजानां विछिन्द्याद् अथो समानपात्रौ ह्य् एतौ सोमौ गृह्येते तस्मान् नानुयजति देवा वै तृतीयसवनम् उद्यमं नाशक्नुवन् प्रातःसवने तर्हि सवितासीत् तं देवास् तृतीयसवनम् अभिपर्यौहंस् तेन तृतीयसवनम् उदयछन्त यत् सावित्रस् तृतीयसवने गृह्यते सवितृप्रसूता वा एतत् तृतीयं सवनम् उद्यछन्ते सावित्रस्य संस्रवे वैश्वदेवम् अभिगृह्णाति वैश्वदेवीर् इमाः प्रजाः सवितृप्रसूताः खलु वै प्रजाः प्रजायन्ते मनो वै सविता वैश्वदेवीर् इमाः प्रजाः सर्वासु वा एतत् प्रजासु मनो दधात्य् आशीर्मतः सवनस्य गृह्णाति वैश्वदेवत्वाय सुशर्मासि सुप्रतिष्ठान इति यत् स्वित् सोमः सोमे प्रतितिष्ठति बृहदुक्षे नमा इति यद् बृहद् इति तेन देवेभ्यो यन् नमा इति तेन पितृभ्य उक्थभाजो वै पितरो ऽस्तोमभाज उक्थायैष गृह्यते न स्तोत्राय यत्र गृह्यते तञ् शस्यते स्व आयतत्ने ॥
4.7.1.m:
Savitṛ, indeed, is connected with the Gāyatrī among the gods.
This Soma is drawn in the place of the Gāyatrī,
namely the Āgrāyaṇa.
Therefore the Sāvitra [cup] is drawn out from the Āgrāyaṇa.
It lies beside [the fire] there until the third pressing,
for the impelling of what is being done again and again.
The Antaryāma [cup], indeed, is the intermediate space.
These creatures are the intermediate space.
In that he draws the Sāvitra [cup] with the Antaryāma vessel,
Savitṛ thereby impels these creatures,
for procreation.
It is offered without being deposited [on the khara];
for these creatures are not deposited, they do not settle down.
He does not offer an after-offering.
If he were to offer an after-offering, he would cut off the propagation of creatures.
Moreover, these two Somas are drawn in the same vessel;
therefore he does not offer an after-offering.
The gods, indeed, could not lift up the third pressing.
Savitṛ was then at the morning pressing.
The gods drove him around towards the third pressing;
by him they lifted up the third pressing.
In that the Sāvitra [cup] is drawn at the third pressing,
impelled by Savitṛ they lift up the third pressing.
He draws the Vaiśvadeva [cup] over the residue of the Sāvitra [cup].
These creatures belong to the Viśve Devāḥ.
Impelled by Savitṛ, indeed, creatures are procreated.
Mind, indeed, is Savitṛ;
these creatures belong to the Viśve Devāḥ.
He thus places mind in all creatures.
He draws from the pressing provided with the milk mixture,
for the sake of the Vaiśvadeva quality.
“You are good shelter, a good resting place,” [he says];
for Soma, indeed, rests upon Soma.
“Homage to the great sprinkler,” [he says];
in that [he says] “great,” thereby [it is] for the gods;
in that [he says] “homage,” thereby [it is] for the fathers.
The fathers, indeed, have a share in the uktha, not in the stotra.
It is drawn for the uktha, not for the stotra.
Where it is drawn, there it is recited,
in its own proper place.

4.7.2.s: ghṛtasya yajaty eṣa vai prathamo dhiṣṇyānāṃ yad āhavanīyas taṃ vā etad agre vyāghārayaty āgnāvaiṣṇavyā vyāghārayati parāṅ vā etarhi yajño 'gniḥ sarvā devatā viṣṇur yajño devatāś caiva yajñaṃ cālabdha ghnanti vā etat somaṃ yad abhiṣuṇvanti yat saumyaḥ somaṃ vā etat saṃbhāvayanti somam āpāyayanty avadhiṣur vā etat somaṃ yad abhyasuṣuvur anustaraṇī vā eṣā somasya yat saumyaḥ pitṝṇām anustaraṇī tasmāt pitṛmatyā yajati dakṣiṇā tiṣṭhan juhoti dakṣiṇā hi pitṝṇām upasadāṃ vā ete 'nuyājā āgnāvaiṣṇavyā ghṛtasya yajati saumyā somasya yā evāda upasatsu devatā ayākṣīt tā etad amutra vā eṣa bhūtāya kriyate yad vā etasya vyārdhi yat prāmāyi tad asyāmuṃ lokaṃ gachaty atha pūta evoñśiṣyate pavitraṃ vai saumyo yajamānam evaitena punāti sāmadevatyo vai somaḥ somasya khalu vai saumyaḥ sāmne vā etad dhriyate || satrā ta etad yad u ta iha || iti paripaśyati yo 'gatāsuḥ sa paripaśyati yo gatāsur na sa paripaśyati yadi na paripaśyed atha vadet || yan me mano yamaṃ gataṃ yad vā me aparāgatam | rājñā somena tad vayam asmāsu dhārayāmasi || hṛdispṛk kratuspṛg varcodhā asi varco me dhehi || iti āśiṣam evāśāste ||
4.7.2.d: घृतस्य यजत्य् एष वै प्रथमो धिष्ण्यानां यद् आहवनीयस् तं वा एतद् अग्रे व्याघारयत्य् आग्नावैष्णव्या व्याघारयति पराङ् वा एतर्हि यज्ञो ऽग्निः सर्वा देवता विष्णुर् यज्ञो देवताश् चैव यज्ञं चालब्ध घ्नन्ति वा एतत् सोमं यद् अभिषुण्वन्ति यत् सौम्यः सोमं वा एतत् संभावयन्ति सोमम् आपाययन्त्य् अवधिषुर् वा एतत् सोमं यद् अभ्यसुषुवुर् अनुस्तरणी वा एषा सोमस्य यत् सौम्यः पितॄणाम् अनुस्तरणी तस्मात् पितृमत्या यजति दक्षिणा तिष्ठन् जुहोति दक्षिणा हि पितॄणाम् उपसदां वा एते ऽनुयाजा आग्नावैष्णव्या घृतस्य यजति सौम्या सोमस्य या एवाद उपसत्सु देवता अयाक्षीत् ता एतद् अमुत्र वा एष भूताय क्रियते यद् वा एतस्य व्यार्धि यत् प्रामायि तद् अस्यामुं लोकं गछत्य् अथ पूत एवोञ्शिष्यते पवित्रं वै सौम्यो यजमानम् एवैतेन पुनाति सामदेवत्यो वै सोमः सोमस्य खलु वै सौम्यः साम्ने वा एतद् ध्रियते ॥ सत्रा त एतद् यद् उ त इह ॥ इति परिपश्यति यो ऽगतासुः स परिपश्यति यो गतासुर् न स परिपश्यति यदि न परिपश्येद् अथ वदेत् ॥ यन् मे मनो यमं गतं यद् वा मे अपरागतम् । राज्ञा सोमेन तद् वयम् अस्मासु धारयामसि ॥ हृदिस्पृक् क्रतुस्पृग् वर्चोधा असि वर्चो मे धेहि ॥ इति आशिषम् एवाशास्ते ॥
4.7.2.m:
He sacrifices with ghee.
This Āhavanīya, indeed, is the first of the dhiṣṇya hearths;
he thus sprinkles it with clarified butter in the beginning.
With a verse to Agni and Viṣṇu he sprinkles [it] with clarified butter.
The sacrifice at that time is turned away.
Agni is all deities;
Viṣṇu is the sacrifice.
He has seized both the deities and the sacrifice.
They kill Soma when they press [it].
In that there is the Saumya [offering],
they thereby restore Soma;
they cause Soma to swell.
They killed Soma when they pressed [it].
This Saumya [cup] is the anustaraṇī cow of Soma;
it is the anustaraṇī cow of the fathers.
Therefore he sacrifices with a verse containing [the name of] the fathers.
Standing towards the south he offers;
for the south belongs to the fathers.
These are the after-offerings of the Upasads.
With a verse to Agni and Viṣṇu he sacrifices of ghee; with a verse to Soma, of Soma.
The deities which he sacrificed to there at the Upasads, those [he sacrifices to] here.
This is done for him who has become [departed] to yonder world.
Whatever of him was destitute, whatever passed away, that goes to yonder world for him.
Then, purified, he is left behind.
The Saumya, indeed, is a purifier;
he thus purifies the sacrificer with it.
Soma belongs to the Sāman as its deity;
the Saumya, indeed, belongs to Soma;
for the Sāman, indeed, it is held.
“Together with this [strength] of yours, which is also here for you,” saying this, he looks around.
He who has his life-breath not departed looks around;
he who has his life-breath departed does not look around.
If he should not look around, then he should say:
“Whatever mind of mine has gone to Yama, or whatever has not departed, / that we hold fast in ourselves by King Soma.”
“Touching the heart, touching the resolve, you are a granter of splendor; / bestow splendor upon me,” he says;
he thus prays for a blessing.
